title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | FBM KLCI rises ahead of Bank Negara's monetary policy decision
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Good morning mooers! Here are things you need to know about today's market:
AI Deals Boost Tech Stocks as Markets Navigate Economic Uncertainties
KLSE Rises on Blue-Chip Buying Despite Broader Market Caution
Stocks to watch: GENTING, CAPITALA, etc.
- Moomoo News MY
Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 6,851.97 (+0.17%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 47,336.68 (-0.48%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 23,834.72 (+0.46%)
The $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ and $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ started November on a positive note, rising 0.17% and 0.46% respectively, driven by a wave of artificial intelligence-related deals. $Amazon (AMZN.US)$ shares hit a new all-time high, climbing 4% after securing a $38 billion multiyear agreement with OpenAI. $IREN Ltd (IREN.US)$ surged 11.52% following a $9.7 billion deal with Microsoft, while $NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$ gained 2.17% on news of U.S. approval to ship chips to the UAE.
Despite the tech sector's strength, the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ fell 0.48%. Investors face significant uncertainty due to ongoing tariffs and economic concerns, compounded by the 34-day government shutdown affecting consumer sentiment. With official government statistics unavailable, market participants are relying on private-sector data and earnings reports for economic insights.
Over 60% of S&P 500 companies have reported earnings, with most beating analyst expectations. However, a recent survey indicates U.S. factory activity unexpectedly retreated in October, and investors are looking to the upcoming ADP jobs report for labor market indicators.
Despite these challenges, some analysts believe the market remains stable as long as private-sector data and earnings reports continue to show strength.
Bursa Market Insight
$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ 1622.42 (+0.82%)
Top Gainer: $MRDIY (5296.MY)$ RM1.650 (+3.13%)
Top Loser: $MISC (3816.MY)$ RM7.650 (-1.80%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.1995 (+0.27%)
The $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ closed at its intraday high of 1,622.42 on Monday, gaining 13.27 points or 0.82%, driven by selective blue-chip buying amidst regional gains. However, the broader market showed weakness with negative breadth, as 762 decliners outnumbered 450 gainers. Trading volume reached 3.25 billion shares worth RM2.48 billion.
Market strength was underpinned by multiple factors. Firstly, "delayed rate cut" optimism emerged following the US Federal Reserve's recent policy easing. Secondly, positive sentiment in the banking sector contributed to the upward momentum. Additionally, renewed buying interest in select blue-chip stocks further reinforced the market's positive tone.
Looking ahead, analysts expect Bank Negara Malaysia to maintain the overnight policy rate at its upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meeting.
IPO Scanner
Stocks to Watch
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ has secured over 50% ownership of Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM), making its takeover offer unconditional. The group now holds 2.84 billion GENM shares, representing 50.105% of GENM's total issued shares. The offer will remain open until November 24, unless extended or revised.
$CAPITALA (5099.MY)$ is considering establishing a Bahrain-based airline to operate narrowbody aircraft in the Middle East, Central Asia, Africa, and Europe. This move is part of the group's expansion strategy, which includes plans to launch flights from Southeast Asian countries to Bahrain over the next five years, with potential connectivity to Europe and the US.
$LCTITAN (5284.MY)$'s third-quarter net loss narrowed to RM197.86 million from RM246.42 million a year earlier. Quarterly revenue rose 26% year-on-year to RM2.45 billion, driven by increased supply to its Indonesian project. The improved performance was supported by stronger sales, lower depreciation charges, and reduced losses from its US associate.
$MAHSING (8583.MY)$ has acquired a 275-acre freehold parcel in Semenyih for RM273.5 million from a S P Setia Bhd subsidiary. The land, adjacent to Mah Sing's existing M Legasi township, will be developed into M Legasi 2. Of the acquired land, 175 acres are earmarked for mixed residential and commercial development with a projected gross development value of RM1.7 billion.
$MMAG (0034.MY)$'s stock hit its limit-down, reaching a 19-month low. The company stated it is unaware of any explanations for the unusual market activity. Concurrently, MMAG announced the resignation of executive director Chin Boon Long, following his spouse's cessation as a substantial shareholder eight months prior. $ZENTECH (0094.MY)$'s plan to acquire a 30% stake in Souqa Fintech Sdn Bhd, a shariah-compliant payment gateway provider, has been terminated. Souqa ended the negotiations on October 28, citing adverse commercial and structural considerations revealed during internal evaluations and due diligence.
$HOHUP (5169.MY)$ must submit its 2025 annual report by November 7 or risk share suspension from November 10. The company missed the end-October deadline but states the report is in its final stages of completion. Ho Hup expects to issue the report by the new deadline, avoiding potential suspension of its securities.
$DESTINI (7212.MY)$ has until November 7 to submit its FY2025 annual report or face trading suspension from November 10. The engineering group, which recently pivoted to the rail sector, missed the October 31 deadline for releasing its report, including audited financial statements and reports.
Buy or Sell?
Source: Dow Jones Newswires, Bursa Malaysia, The Malaysian Reserve, The Star, The Edge.

author: 心如紫水
body: Your question is highly pertinent. In fact—this is indeed one of the most commonly used, and also the most ‘subtle and sophisticated’ strategies employed by many major shareholders in privatization operations. Let us conduct a detailed analysis of the possibility and rationale behind Lim Kok Thay’s approach of 'final-stage consolidation of allied votes' 👇 ⸻ 🧩 1. Theoretically: Entirely possible In practical mergers and acquisitions operations, such an approach of **‘delayed formal consolidation (final consolidation)’** does exist. The operational logic is as follows: 1. Early stage: Strategic positioning and dispersed shareholding • If the major shareholder (e.g., Lim Kok Thay) has long intended to privatize, they will first purchase shares through trusted associates, family members, or long-term cooperative funds. • These ‘allies’ will temporarily not declare their shares as 'acting in concert,' as on the surface, they appear to be independent investors. 2. Before the official announcement: Maintain distance to avoid triggering a Mandatory General Offer (MGO). • According to Malaysian regulations, once the combined shareholding of parties acting in concert exceeds 33%, a full takeover offer must be made. • Therefore, before the official announcement, these allies generally keep their total holdings below the 'safe threshold' of 32.99% to avoid triggering regulatory requirements. 3. After the official announcement: 'Recover' shares during the public offer phase. • Once Lim Kok Thay formally makes an acquisition offer (e.g., RM2.35), those allies can nominally 'accept the offer' and sell their shares to him. • From a market perspective, this is seen as 'ordinary shareholders responding to the acquisition'; from a strategic perspective, this represents 'recouping votes within one’s own camp.' • This approach avoids violating disclosure requirements while safely and legally integrating 'private arrangements' under one's own name. 4. Final Outcome • Before the official announcement: Hidden control, avoiding regulatory triggers. • After the official announcement: Legal integration to achieve target shareholding levels. ⸻ ⚖️ II. The Boundary Between Legality and the Gray Area The key to this approach lies in the following: • As long as the regulatory authority (SC Malaysia) cannot prove that these allies are “acting in concert,” it remains gray but compliant. • However, if evidence (funding sources, common directors, communication records) indicates that these individuals were instructed to purchase, it may be deemed a violation retroactively. In other words: ⚠️ “The final collection of ally votes” is a clever but high-risk strategy, Once幕后 coordination is exposed, it may violate Rule 216 of the Takeover and Merger Code. ⸻ 📈 III. Practical Reference: The Personality and Past Practices of Lim Kok Thay Based on past cases (such as the 2019 acquisition of Genting Hong Kong assets or earlier equity adjustments in Genting Singapore), Lim Kok Thay’s consistent strategy has been: • First, stabilize the situation (acquiring shares up to a safe threshold) • Then, announce the news officially (triggering a rise in stock price) • Finally, integrate gradually and recoup investments slowly This demonstrates that he is a highly disciplined capital operator who excels at leveraging timing gaps and regulatory loopholes. Therefore, if asked, 'Will he wait until the last moment to buy back friendly shares?' my view is: ✅ Highly likely. Moreover, he most likely planned the 'post-announcement share acquisition pathway' long ago. ⸻ 🔍 IV. Three signals you can observe If you want to verify whether he is really in the 'final stage of collecting friendly votes,' you can pay attention to the following in the coming weeks: 1. Changes in shareholding ratio • If he or Kien Huat rapidly increases their stake on the open market in a short period (e.g., from 50% → 55% → 60%), it indicates that votes are being quickly consolidated. 2. Trading volume characteristics • If there is a sudden surge in trading volume but the identity of the seller remains undisclosed, it is highly likely that friendly accounts are 'cashing out.' 3. A sharp increase in filings just days before the offer period ends • Typically, as the offer approaches its deadline, a group of major shareholders will 'concentrate on accepting the offer,' which often reflects pre-arranged strategies.

• Wall Street Rallies as U.S. Government Shutdown Nears End
• Fed's Miran Advocates for 50 Basis Point Rate Cut in December

• Stocks to watch: MRDIY, SUNREIT, etc.
🇺🇸Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 6,832.43 (+1.54%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 47368.63 (+0.81%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 23,527.17 (+2.27%)
U.S. stock markets rebounded on Monday, with technology stocks leading the charge. The $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ surged 2.27% or 522.64 points, closing at 23,537.17, as tech giants like $Palantir (PLTR.US)$, $NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$, $Alphabet-C (GOOG.US)$, and $Tesla (TSLA.US)$ recovered from last week's losses. The broader $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ gained 1.54% or 103.63 points to end at 6,832.43, while the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ rose 0.81% or 381.53 points to 47,368.63.
U.S. stocks rebounded Monday as progress towards ending the 41-day government shutdown boosted investor sentiment. A key procedural vote passed in the Senate with 61 votes, including support from eight Democrats, signaling a potential resolution to the budget impasse.
The breakthrough came after Democrats compromised on healthcare subsidies, while Republicans agreed to future votes on extending these subsidies and reversing certain Trump-era policies. While final procedural steps remain, the government is expected to reopen within days, contributing to a risk-on mood across Wall Street.
Federal Reserve Governor Stephan Miran, known for his dovish stance, reinforced market optimism by reiterating his support for a significant interest rate cut at the Fed's December meeting. During a CNBC TV appearance, Miran stated that a 50 basis point reduction would be appropriate, barring new information, while emphasizing that a minimum 25 basis point cut should be considered.

The Malaysian stock market closed higher on Monday, with the $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ rising 8.25 points or 0.51% to 1,627.38. This uptick was driven by a combination of positive domestic and global factors. Locally, investor confidence was boosted by signs of a resilient labor market and a firming ringgit. Globally, Asian equities rallied on news of progress towards ending the US government shutdown, with the US Senate passing the first stage of a deal late Sunday night.
Malaysia's stock market performance strengthened on the back of positive economic indicators, according to Mohd Sedek Jantan, an investment strategist. The latest labour force data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) demonstrated robust domestic fundamentals, signaling a sustained recovery in household demand.
This, coupled with the ringgit's appreciation and stable macroeconomic indicators, has bolstered investor sentiment. Sedek highlighted the interplay between domestic strength and improving global macro signals, suggesting that Malaysia's equity market is well-positioned for continued upward momentum into the final quarter of 2025.

title: Independent Advisor: Offer Unfair and Unreasonable; Recommend Rejection of Genting Malaysia Privatization
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 13th Report) Independent advisor Kenanga Investment Bank believes that the major shareholder, Genting,$GENTING (3182.MY)$ Offer to acquire all shares of Genting Malaysia at MYR 2.35 per share,$GENM (4715.MY)$ is "unfair and unreasonable," and recommends other shareholders reject the offer.
Kenanga Investment Bank’s independent research report released today highlights that the full acquisition price of MYR 2.35 per share, compared with Genting Malaysia's valuation using the Sum-of-the-Parts Valuation (SOPV) method, indicates a per-share value between MYR 3.48 and MYR 3.77, reflecting a discount of 32.47% to 37.67%.
At the same time, compared to the highest values over the past one year and two years, it reflects a relative discount of 3.69% to 19.52%; however, against the volume-weighted average price (VWAP) over more than two years, it shows a premium of 2.58%.
In view of this, Kenanga Investment Bank believes that the aforementioned acquisition is 'unfair.'
Active trading should not lead to delisting.
On the other hand, as the offeror, Genting also has no intention of maintaining the listing status of Genting Malaysia. However, given the active trading of Genting Malaysia over the past two months, it remains uncertain whether the offeror will be able to reach the 90% threshold required to apply for delisting. Therefore, Kenanga Investment Bank considers this acquisition 'unreasonable.'
The report mentioned that, as of November 6, the offeror held a total of 2.84033 billion shares in Genting Malaysia, equivalent to 50.11% of the latter's equity.
In other words, as long as Genting Malaysia continues to meet the public shareholding requirement and the offeror’s stake does not exceed 90%, its shares can continue to be traded on the main board.
It is worth noting that, as of September 2025, Genting Malaysia's average monthly trading volume over the past 24 months reached 193 million shares, accounting for 7.1% of the market's free float, reflecting active trading and liquidity even better than the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI's 6.48%.
After comprehensive consideration, Kenanga Investment Bank issued an 'unfair and unreasonable' recommendation and urged minority shareholders to reject the privatization proposal.
Independent directors maintain a unified position
Moreover, after evaluating the terms of the full acquisition and referencing Kenanga Investment Bank’s report, Genting Malaysia’s independent directors agreed that the offer is 'unfair' and 'unreasonable' to the company’s shareholders.
The independent directors pointed out that the full acquisition price does not adequately reflect the value of the company’s assets and its long-term growth potential, and lacks sufficient attractiveness to safeguard the best interests of minority shareholders.
Therefore, the independent directors unanimously recommended that shareholders reject the full acquisition offer and fully consider Genting Malaysia’s fundamentals and the potential for future business development before making a decision.
Converted into an unconditional full offer
As the full offer progresses, Genting has continued to increase its stake in Genting Malaysia at prices below the offer price of MYR 2.35 over the past five trading days. Its current shareholding has now exceeded 55%.
According to the announcement issued by Genting, as of November 13, the company had purchased a total of 34,929,300 shares, or 2.02% of Genting Malaysia's equity, through open market transactions at a full purchase price not exceeding MYR 2.35 per share.
To date, Genting holds 3,231,070,000 shares in Genting Malaysia, equivalent to 57.008% of its equity.
The deadline has been extended to December 1.
In view of this, Genting’s original conditional full takeover offer will become an unconditional full acquisition offer; meanwhile, the original deadline for the full acquisition will be extended from November 24 to 5:00 PM on December 1.
Spurred by the news of the full acquisition, Genting Malaysia’s trading volume in the market was highly active. Its stock price once rose to MYR 2.36, surpassing the full acquisition price of MYR 2.35 per share; however, it later retreated and closed flat at MYR 2.35, aligning with the privatization offer price.
As reported earlier, Genting plans to acquire all remaining shares of Genting Malaysia at MYR 2.35 per share, or up to MYR 6.7446 billion, and subsequently delist the latter through privatization.
Analysts have differing views
Genting’s plan to fully acquire and privatize Genting Malaysia has elicited different opinions among analysts.
Maybank Investment Banking analysts believe that the above offer did not take into account three major future benefits for Genting Malaysia, and the share price may rise as high as MYR 3.28. Genting needs to significantly increase its offer price to be fair, thus recommending shareholders to reject the offer.
Additionally, although TA Securities analysts agree that Genting’s full acquisition price is unattractive, they believe that it is unlikely that Genting will increase its offer.
The likelihood of Genting raising its offer is low, as the board of Genting Malaysia has no need to seek additional competitive acquisition proposals. Therefore, this offer may not receive sufficient support, and Genting Malaysia may ultimately fail to be privatized and delisted.
However, analysts at Galaxy International Securities hold a different view, suggesting that shareholders should accept the offer since Genting's bid is higher than their target price of MYR 1.88, providing shareholders with a decent exit opportunity.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | US government shutdown ends, but October inflation data lost and job report incomplete
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Key Takeaways:
• US Stock Market Tumbles as Tech and Non-Tech Sectors Face Broad Sell-Off
• US Government Shutdown Ends, but Economic Data Uncertainty Persists
• Bursa Malaysia Closes Marginally Higher After Choppy Trading Session
• Malaysian Market Sentiment Improves Amid Foreign Buying and Global Developments
• Stocks to watch: GENTING, PHARMA, etc.
🇺🇸Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 6,737.49 (-1.66%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 47,457.22 (-1.65%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 22,870.36 (-2.29%)
Major US stock indexes experienced significant declines on Thursday, with the $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ leading the downturn, falling 2.29% to 22,870.36. The $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ dropped 1.66% to 6,737.49, while the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ fell 1.65% to 47,457.22.
The sell-off was broad-based, affecting both tech and non-tech sectors. Notable declines were seen in Big Tech companies like $Tesla (TSLA.US)$(-6.64%), $NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$(-3.58%), and $SanDisk Corp (SNDK.US)$(-16.96%), while non-tech Dow components such as $Goldman Sachs (GS.US)$ (-3.99%) and $Disney (DIS.US)$ (-7.75%) also suffered losses.
The 43-day U.S. government shutdown ended Wednesday night, with federal workers returning to their jobs on Thursday. However, the impact on economic data reporting remains significant. The White House announced that the October inflation report might never be released, and while the October nonfarm payrolls numbers will be published, the unemployment rate won't be compiled.
This data uncertainty has affected Federal Reserve decision-making, with Fed Chair Jerome Powell indicating it could influence the likelihood of a rate cut in December. The CME FedWatch tool now estimates the probability of a 25-point rate cut at the Fed's December meeting at 49.6%, down from 95.5% a month ago.
🇲🇾Bursa Market Insight
$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ 1632.27 (+0.04%)
Top Gainer: $99SMART (5326.MY)$ RM3.200 (+1.91%)
Top Loser: $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$RM3.790 (-2.57%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.1290 (-0.17%)
The $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ ended slightly higher on Thursday, gaining 0.66 points or 0.04% to close at 1,632.27, supported by banking and consumer stocks. The index experienced a volatile session, fluctuating between 1,631.15 and 1,635.27.
Despite the main index's positive close, losers outnumbered gainers 550 to 480. Market turnover improved to 3.95 billion units worth RM2.77 billion, reflecting increased trading activity compared to the previous day.
IPPFA Sdn Bhd director Mohd Sedek Jantan reported a constructive market sentiment in Malaysia, noting that foreign investors turned net buyers from Monday to Wednesday. This positive trend coincided with the strengthening of the ringgit. Globally, market sentiment improved following the reopening of the US government after President Donald Trump signed a bill passed by the House of Representatives.
🔍IPO Scanner
🔔Stocks to Watch
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ has extended its voluntary takeover offer for $GENM (4715.MY)$ to December 1, now owning 57.008% of GENM's shares. The offer, at RM2.35 per share, turned unconditional on November 3.
$PHARMA (7081.MY)$'s net profit plummeted 92.8% to RM7.28 million in Q3 FY2025, attributed to increased transport costs for delivering new products to East Malaysia. Revenue slightly decreased by 2.19% to RM1 billion, with no dividend declared for the quarter.
$OCK (0172.MY)$ is set to acquire Edotco Group's telecom tower operations in Laos and will build 30 new tower sites. The purchase price remains undisclosed, with no official filing to Bursa Malaysia yet.
REV Media Group, a subsidiary of $MEDIA (4502.MY)$, has completed the full acquisition of The Vocket Sdn Bhd, a Malay-language lifestyle and culture platform. REV Media acquired the remaining 48% equity interest, solidifying its position in the Malay digital media market.
$CITAGLB (7245.MY)$ has won a RM628 million contract from Jabatan Bekalan Air Malaysia for a raw water and flood mitigation project in Selangor. The 48-month design-and-build project includes constructing a weir, installing raw water pipelines, and upgrading 10 existing ponds, showcasing Citaglobal's involvement in major infrastructure development.
$DPHARMA (7148.MY)$ reported a 44.7% rise in Q3 net profit to RM22.57 million, with revenue up 6.6% to RM222.48 million. The improved performance was driven by a favorable product mix and strengthening ringgit, enhancing overall margins.
$CARLSBG (2836.MY)$ posted a net profit of RM103.03 million for Q3 2025, with revenue increasing 4.9% to RM583.37 million. The company declared a 25 sen interim dividend but expressed concerns about the potential impact of excise duty increases on consumer demand and illicit alcohol consumption.
$DLADY (3026.MY)$ reported an 86.1% jump in Q3 net profit to RM32.06 million, with revenue rising 5.4% to RM374.52 million. The growth was attributed to strong liquid milk sales, professional channel growth, and new product contributions.
$SPSETIA (8664.MY)$'s Q3 net profit fell 32% to RM68.03 million, with revenue declining 30.71% to RM872.26 million. The decrease was due to lower property development earnings and reduced land sales, despite a 78% year-on-year sales growth.

body:
Retail investors remain retail investors, even though they have moved away from GENM; fundamentally, they are still the same. Esteemed colleagues, we are GENT, not GENM. If you come here expecting to continue with the same GENM mindset—buying shares at 50% discount while still receiving dividends like the parent stock, and then complaining that LKT is taking advantage of you—perhaps GENT is not the right fit for you.

There is no point in blaming the capitalists here because we are the parent company. Unlike GENM, which can blame its parent company, LKT, or any external factor, they ultimately do nothing but talk. GENM’s acquisition of EMPIRE was aimed at packaging it together with GENUS and RWLV for a potential listing in the United States after the acquisition is completed. However, there is no use explaining this to you people from GENM since all you care about are dividends, Uncle Lim, and GENT doing what you want.

Now that you claim to have switched to GENT, please take a moment to reflect: Is it really as satisfying as you imagine to say that LKT has been forced into retreat? If GENT doesn’t perform well and you’re holding expensive shares, do you genuinely believe your investment in GENT will fare better? If you want to cling to the GENM mindset where you expect LKT to act against you and derive satisfaction only when you see losses, perhaps you would be better suited exploring other tickers.

author: Lucas Cheah
body:
Genting is one of Malaysia’s most well-known conglomerates. It operates across several areas, but its biggest businesses are in hospitality, resorts, casinos, and gaming. It also has exposure to plantations, energy, and property, but the core income still comes from its entertainment and tourism operations, mainly through Resorts World Genting.

1. How the company makes money

• Resorts & Gaming
Income from casino operations, hotel stays, food & beverage, theme parks, and entertainment. This is the group’s strongest and most stable income source, especially during holiday or travel seasons.

• Plantation & Property
Genting also earns from palm oil estates and property development, but these contribute a smaller share compared to the resorts business.

• Energy & Power
Some income comes from power generation assets, though this segment tends to be more volatile.

2. What to watch in the upcoming earnings

• Visitor numbers at Resorts World Genting
Higher foot traffic usually means stronger spending on gaming, hotels, and entertainment. Public holidays and tourism trends will play a big role.

• Gaming revenue performance
Any improvement or slowdown in casino activity will have a direct impact on the company’s results.

• Cost management
Energy prices, staff costs, and maintenance expenses can affect profit margins. Look out for whether the company is keeping costs under control.

• Recovery of regional markets
Genting also operates overseas (Singapore, UK, US). Results from these markets, especially Singapore could lift or drag overall earnings.

• Updates on new projects or expansions
Any progress on new attractions or upgrades at Genting Highlands could influence future earnings potential.

3. Risks and challenges

• Heavy reliance on tourism and gaming
If economic conditions weaken or travel demand drops, Genting may feel the impact quickly.

• High operating costs
Running a large resort involves significant expenses. Rising wages, utilities, or maintenance costs can squeeze profits.

• Regulatory changes
Gaming is highly regulated. Any new rules, license conditions, or tax adjustments could affect earnings.

• Competition from regional casino hubs
Nearby markets like Singapore and Macau may pull tourists away if their offerings become more attractive.

4. Summary
Genting’s upcoming earnings will mainly be driven by how well Resorts World Genting performed, especially in gaming and tourism-related activities. If visitor numbers remain strong and spending stays healthy, the company should deliver steady results. However, investors should keep an eye on cost pressures and any changes in the tourism outlook.

Overall, Genting remains a long-standing player in Malaysia’s leisure and entertainment sector, with earnings largely tied to how much people are willing to travel, stay, and spend at its resorts.

author: Mappygital
body:
Key Performance Drivers
1. Resorts World Genting (RWG) gaming volume:
RWG remains the core revenue engine, with mass-market gaming activity rebounding post-pandemic. FY25 saw a 19% YoY revenue increase in Malaysia driven by higher
footfall.

2. International expansion:
Genting’s US and Bahamas operations surged 64% in revenue in 3Q25, boosted by Empire Resorts consolidation. This diversification helps offset domestic volatility.

3. Tourism recovery:
Malaysia’s push for 36 million visitors under Visit Malaysia 2026 is expected to lift RWG footfall, especially from China, India, and Singapore.

4. EBITDA margin improvement:
Despite cost pressures, Genting’s adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 31% in 3Q25, showing operational leverage as volumes scale.

5. Strategic acquisitions:
The buyout of Empire Resorts and Genting Casino Stratford adds scale and long-term upside, though integration costs remain a short-term drag.

Key Risks to Monitor
1. Foreign exchange losses:
Genting’s 3Q25 net profit fell 79% YoY largely due to weaker forex gains, especially from the pound and USD against MYR.

2. Empire Resorts drag:
The US unit remains loss-making. Genting’s acquisition of the remaining 51% stake adds exposure to a high-cost, low-margin asset.

3. Rising payroll and operating costs:
UK and Egypt EBITDA fell 17% in 3Q25 due to higher expenses, which could pressure margins if not offset by volume growth.

4. Regulatory and tax shifts:
Gaming taxes, ESG mandates, or policy changes in Malaysia or overseas could impact profitability.

5. Economic slowdown:
Genting’s US operations face risk from slower local growth, which could dampen discretionary spending and casino visits.

body:
⭐ Genting Berhad (3182) Most Balanced Overall Assessment:

✅ 1. It is a large conglomerate with a solid foundation but unstable growth.

Genting is a typical company characterized by 'large operations, strong cash flow, but highly volatile business activities.'
• Diversified assets (resorts, entertainment, energy, shipping, gaming, plantations, etc.)
• Decent earning capacity
• However, profitability is often unstable and susceptible to foreign exchange fluctuations and tourism cycles.

Advantages: Low risk of sudden collapse, but explosive growth is also unlikely.

⸻

⚠️ 2. Current major issues: Declining profitability + relatively high debt levels

In recent quarters, Genting has faced several practical pressures:
• Foreign exchange losses
• Rising costs
• Overseas operations (UK, US) showing instability
• Expansion plans require funding (but unstable profitability → increased pressure)
• Debt remains a long-term burden for the company

This indicates that strong financial reports are not guaranteed in the short term.

⸻

🔥 3. Only two key factors will determine the future of the stock price:

(A) Can the financial reports stop deteriorating?

If the next financial report shows at least “no further deterioration,” the market will breathe a sigh of relief, and the stock price may rebound.

(B) New York casino license in the United States

The most significant future 'prize' for Genting is this. If obtained:
• Stock prices may surge immediately
• The parent company (3182) will benefit the most
• This is what the market truly values

However, the license is highly competitive, politically sensitive, and time-consuming, with very high uncertainty.

⸻

🧊 4. Currently more akin to a 'value-oriented + event-driven' stock

What does it mean?
• It is not a high-growth stock
• Its stock price is driven by two factors:
(1) The pace of business recovery → Earnings reports
(2) News about new projects/casino licenses → Events

Therefore: Short-term volatility will be very high, but it is unlikely to become worthless in the long term.

⸻

🎯 5. Balanced conclusion (the key point you are looking for):

⭐ Short-term (1–3 months): Likely to be volatile or slightly weak

Earnings reports may not be strong, and market confidence is moderate, so the short-term outlook is not necessarily optimistic.

⭐ Medium-term (6–12 months): Depends on U.S. licensing + tourism industry performance
• If there is positive news regarding the New York license → Significant increase
• If not → Relatively ordinary, following the gradual recovery of tourism

⭐ Long-term (1–3 years): Stable, but not explosive growth

Genting will not disappear, but it is not a tech stock and will not surge multiple times. It is more akin to:

✔ Stable asset
✔ Gradual recovery in cash flow
✔ Dividend/long-term value-oriented
✔ Major events (licensing) may bring pleasant surprises

⸻

📌 In summary:

Genting (3182) will not deteriorate, but for significant gains, you need to wait for two factors: business recovery + licensing progress.
Short-term volatility, medium-term reliance on policy, and long-term stability but without excessive exuberance.

body:
✅ Current Background/Pressure and Positive Factors

• Recent weak performance

In the third quarter ended September 30, 2025, the company's net profit plummeted to only approximately RM 30.3 million, marking a ~86% year-on-year drop. Despite a rise in revenue, profitability was significantly pressured by foreign exchange losses, reduced interest income, and higher depreciation expenses. (The Edge Malaysia)

This has created uncertainty in the company’s short-term profitability and cash flow situation, potentially making the market more cautious. (The Edge Malaysia)

• Stock price range and low valuation

According to publicly available data, the current share price is within the lower range of the past 52 weeks. (KLSE Screener)

From the perspective of 'Net Asset Value (NAV)', there is a certain gap between the company's book value and market price — which may be attractive to long-term value investors. (KLSE Screener)

• Holding structure and strategic moves — potential implications for the future

The group recently initiated a full takeover/privatization plan for its another listed entity, Genting Malaysia Bhd (GENM), which could lead to significant changes in the group’s structure and asset allocation. (Malay Mail)

• Uncertainty remains in the industry and macro environment.

The group’s business depends on tourism, entertainment, gaming, hotels, etc., making it sensitive to economic conditions, tourist flows, exchange rates, policies, and interest rates. The current instability in currency, interest rates, and the global economic environment will lead to fluctuations in performance.

In light of recent profit declines and external environmental pressures, the market holds a cautious outlook on short-term recovery.

- Mild rebound: If internal restructuring or asset integration gains market recognition + macro environment stabilizes somewhat + no worsening in exchange rates or interest rates, the stock price may recover to mid-term resistance levels (supportive of valuation).
- Range-bound fluctuation: The market awaits the next quarterly earnings report or details of privatization/restructuring, adopting a wait-and-see approach; stock prices may fluctuate within the current range with limited short-term upside.
- Continued decline: If profitability deteriorates, debt pressures emerge, and the macro environment worsens, the stock price may test previous lows or fall further.
- Structural rebound (long-term positive trigger): If successful restructuring leads to asset integration + stabilized operations + investors reassess value, the stock price may exceed current low valuations, though this typically occurs beyond a three-month timeframe.

🎯 My assessment (leaning towards 'cautious — moderately optimistic')

Based on currently available information, I believe that within the next three months, the most likely scenario is range-bound fluctuation with occasional minor rebounds. A very strong upward movement is unlikely unless the group announces positive progress in restructuring or business improvements. If there are no negative developments, the stock price may stabilize at current levels; otherwise, further downside is possible if impacted by macro or operational challenges.

If I were you — remain cautiously positioned for the short term unless you are willing to bear significant volatility risk; otherwise, it is advisable to stay on the sidelines or build positions gradually. For medium- to long-term investments, consider opportunities arising from asset restructuring and valuation recovery.

author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Key Takeaways:
• US Stocks Set for Half-Day Trading Session Tonight Following Thanksgiving Break
• Petronas-Linked Slide Drags Bursa Malaysia Lower in Cautious Trade
• Malaysia's Producer Price Index Drops Softly in October
• Stocks to watch: RHB Bank, YTL Power, etc.
🇺🇸Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 6,812.61 (+0.69%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 47,427.12 (+0.67%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 23,214.69 (+0.82%)
US markets were closed for Thanksgiving on Thursday, with a shortened session scheduled for Friday. The S&P 500 is currently 1.1% below its record high, while the volatility index has hit a three-week low. JPMorgan economists now expect the Fed to cut rates next month, reversing their short-lived call for a delay until January.
🇲🇾Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1617.46 (-0.43%)
Top Gainer: $SIME (4197.MY)$ RM2.01 (+6.35%)
Top Loser: $PETDAG (5681.MY)$ RM20.12 (-3.36%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.1314 (-0.11%)
The $富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ fell 7.04 points, or 0.43% to 1,617.46. Bursa Malaysia declined on Thursday, dragged by PETRONAS-linked stocks and a cautious market mood.
Dealers noted that traders are maintaining a selective stance and expect the ongoing flow of corporate earnings to keep offering short-term opportunities.
Malaysia's producer price index (PPI) declined 0.1% year-on-year in October, improving from the 0.8% drop recorded in September, according to data released Thursday by the Department of Statistics Malaysia.
Despite ongoing global uncertainties, Malaysia’s economy is still projected to grow in 2026, though at a more moderate pace, as key indicators show no signs of an imminent recession, economists say. Most economists forecast that Malaysia's economy will grow by 4.3% to 4.7% year-on-year in 2026. The economic growth rate for the first nine months of 2025 stood at 4.7%.
🔍IPO Scanner
🔔Stocks to Watch
$INARI (0166.MY)$ saw its first-quarter net profit surge 113.5% year-on-year to RM51.5 million, up from RM24.1 million, largely driven by favourable foreign-exchange moves. Revenue for Q1 2026 slid 16% to RM325.8 million from RM388 million, as weaker demand and reduced customer orders cut loading volumes across all segments.
$YTL (4677.MY)$ posted a 3.8% rise in net profit to RM346.48 million for Q1 2026, up from RM333.71 million a year ago, even as revenue dipped 1.7% to RM7.64 billion from RM7.77 billion.
$YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$—majority-owned by YTL Corp with a 52.46% stake—lifted first-quarter net profit 6.4% to RM500.57 million from RM470.6 million a year earlier, even as revenue eased 5.7% to RM5.36 billion from RM5.68 billion.
$HLBANK (5819.MY)$’s net profit remained flat at RM1.09 billion, or 53.2 sen per share, as increased impairment losses and weaker associate income outweighed lower operating expenses.
$RHBBANK (1066.MY)$ posted a record quarterly net profit of RM904 million for Q3 2025, up 8.5% year-on-year, lifted by stronger non-interest income and a sharp drop in credit-loss provisions. Year-on-year, net interest income grew 0.8% while non-interest income expanded 4.6%.
$SIME (4197.MY)$ reported on Thursday that first-quarter net profit fell 56% year-on-year to RM355 million, as the prior-year figure had been lifted by a one-off gain from a land sale. Revenue for Q3 2025 eased to RM18.03 billion from RM18.26 billion.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ reported an 86.5% plunge in Q3 2025 net profit to RM30.3 million (from RM223.8 million last year), hit by smaller forex gains, lower interest income and higher depreciation, even as revenue rose 14.25% to RM7.48 billion.
$GENM (4715.MY)$ saw its third-quarter net profit plunge 79% year-on-year, dragged down by a steep drop in unrealised foreign-exchange gains. Profit for Q3 2025 came in at RM119.7 million versus RM569.2 million a year ago, after forex-related income collapsed to RM2.8 million from RM601.8 million. Top-line momentum stayed strong, however, with revenue rising 22% to RM3.36 billion from RM2.75 billion.
$AXIATA (6888.MY)$ swung to a RM27.35 million net loss in the third quarter after it took a heavy impairment on the value of its assets. Revenue at Malaysia’s largest telecom operator by sales eased roughly 5% year-on-year to RM2.92 billion for the three months ended 30 September 2025.
$MALAKOF (5264.MY)$ reported a 67.5% drop in net profit to RM28.21 million for Q3 2025, down from RM86.88 million a year ago, as a steam-turbine pipe leak at the Tanjung Bin Energy plant cut energy payments.
$BJCORP (3395.MY)$ logged a sixth-consecutive quarterly loss after tax charges wiped out operating profit. The net deficit for Q1 2026 narrowed sharply to RM10.94 million from RM167.85 million a year earlier, helped by smaller foreign-exchange losses, according to a stock-exchange filing. Quarterly revenue advanced 3.6 % year-on-year to RM2.31 billion.

title: New York casino license and privatization deadlines coincide; could Genting Malaysia's acquisition price increase?
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 28th) Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ recently delivered a weak earnings performance, drawing market attention to the announcement of the New York casino license results on December 1. Some reiterated that Genting's $GENTING (3182.MY)$ privatization offer price of MYR 2.35 does not reflect the potential value associated with the New York casino license.
Maybank Investment Bank analysts noted in their earnings report that due to seasonally higher expenses at Resorts World Genting (RWG), coupled with reduced winter visitors to its West Coast US operations, Genting Malaysia’s EBITDA for the fourth quarter is expected to weaken on a quarter-on-quarter basis.
However, he also stated that the market is now focused on the outcome of Resorts World New York City (RWNYC) casino license in New York's downstate commercial casino bidding and estimates that expansion-related profits will peak in 2030 at approximately MYR 1.93 billion.
The analyst reiterated his recommendation that shareholders reject the mandatory general offer (MGO) at MYR 2.35 per share, expressing confidence that Genting Malaysia will secure the casino license, a value not reflected in the MYR 2.35 acquisition price.
Genting's stake increases to 63.38%
On another note, Public Investment Bank analysts mentioned that Genting has extended the deadline for its voluntary offer from November 24 to December 1, coinciding with the day the New York State Gaming Commission (NYSGC) will announce the results of the casino license bidding.
“If Genting fails to achieve sufficient acceptance rates, it may need to raise its offer price, especially if Genting Malaysia successfully secures the casino license.”
The analyst also added that Genting Malaysia’s independent advisor has recommended shareholders to reject the MYR 2.35 offer, deeming it “unfair” and “unreasonable.”
According to the Bursa Malaysia announcement, Genting's shareholding in Genting Malaysia as of yesterday was 63.38%.
CIMB Investment Bank analysts also noted that Resorts World New York's Q3 EBITDA fell by 13% year-on-year due to the casino clearing some gaming spaces to install new gaming tables and slot machines after securing the casino license.
Core earnings forecasts significantly upgraded
“Resorts World Genting’s Q3 revenue increased by 22% year-on-year, with EBITDA margins expanding by 2.1 percentage points. We have raised our core EPS forecasts for fiscal years 2025 to 2027 by 58% to 69% to reflect these positive developments.”
Maybank Investment Bank maintained its 'Buy' rating on Genting Malaysia, raising the target price from MYR 2.91 to MYR 3.27; Public Investment Bank reiterated its 'Short-term Buy' rating, increasing the target price from MYR 1.84 to MYR 2.35; CIMB Investment Bank maintained its 'Hold' rating, revising the target price upwards from MYR 2.35 to MYR 2.55.
However, Maybank Investment Bank and CIMB Investment Bank also indicated that if Genting Malaysia wins the New York casino license, their respective target prices could increase by 47 sen and 52 sen.

title: Genting Malaysia's privatization falls short, brokers anticipate a second wave of actions
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
Genting Malaysia Privatization Falls Short of Requirements Securities firms anticipate a second wave of actions. Reported by Lin Disheng Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ full acquisition and privatization of Genting Malaysia $GENM (4715.MY)$ The offer, which concluded at 5 p.m. today, resulted in Genting raising its stake to 73.133%, but it failed to meet the 90% threshold required for completing the privatization. Market observers believe that Genting may subsequently raise its bid and continue pursuing the privatization of Genting Malaysia. According to the announcement, as of 5 p.m. today, Genting holds a total of 4.144 billion shares or 73.133% of Genting Malaysia's equity, an increase from 2.833 billion shares or 49.999% when the full acquisition offer was made, representing an additional 1.311 billion shares or 23.134%. Nevertheless, the above-mentioned shareholding ratio not only falls short of the 90% mandatory general offer threshold but also remains below 75%, indicating that the public float is still above the minimum regulatory requirement of 25% for listing. Huang Zhuhao, Founder and CEO of Tradeview Capital, pointed out in a telephone interview with Nanyang Siang Pau that although this privatization attempt has fallen through, Genting is likely to raise its offer further to push forward with the privatization of Genting Malaysia. “Considering that Genting has made significant efforts for the privatization plan, even resorting to debt financing to secure the acquisition funds, I believe that Genting is determined to privatize Genting Malaysia, and therefore, it is very likely to further increase its offer going forward.” An increase in the offer price to MYR 2.80 is anticipated. He predicted that Genting may subsequently raise its bid to between MYR 2.50 and MYR 2.80. Previously, Genting announced a bid of MYR 2.35 per share, or a total of MYR 6.7 billion, for a full takeover of Genting Malaysia. Ng Huang Han also noted that if Genting merely intended to increase its stake in Genting Malaysia to strengthen control, there would be no need to go through the trouble of pursuing a privatization plan. He believed that Genting’s decision to privatize might be based on two considerations. “Genting may feel that Genting Malaysia’s value has been significantly undervalued, and there is no need for both companies to be listed simultaneously. Moreover, after privatization, Genting Malaysia will have greater flexibility to expand in the U.S. market without being constrained by Bursa Malaysia.” Huang Han also pointed out that the outcome of the bidding process for casino licenses in New York's lower state will further clarify the prospects for Genting Malaysia. The local government of New York will announce the results of the bidding process for the casino licenses on December 1, local time. As Genting Malaysia is one of the three remaining bidders, and the New York State government may issue three licenses, the market believes that the company is almost certain to win.

title: Finally, GenM has successfully secured the gaming license in New York! Could this be Tan Sri’s ultimate plan behind insisting on privatizing GenM? The GenM
author: 心如紫水
body:
Finally, GenM has successfully secured the gaming license in New York! Could this be Tan Sri’s ultimate plan behind insisting on privatizing GenM? The GenM Resorts World project is the largest of the three casino proposals in terms of investment scale, amounting to USD 5.5 billion, and has the potential to become one of the largest casinos in New York. On the other hand, it was once thought that achieving a 75% ownership stake for Genting's privatization would be a distant goal. However, within less than two months, Tan Sri directly increased his stake to 73%, leaving only 2% remaining before reaching the 75% threshold required for delisting. With just an additional MYR 200-300 million spent on acquiring shares, the company could go private. But anyhow, the RM2.35 offer was officially closed at 5 PM yesterday. This means that starting today, there is a possibility of significant volatility in Genting's share price. However, if I remember correctly, GenM should still be able to extend its offer until January next year, but it remains uncertain whether Tan Sri will choose to do so. In the event that GenM does proceed with the delisting, shareholders will have to fend for themselves. That said, there have been some previous instances of privatization and delisting: with the absence of a large number of retail investors, only insiders remain, and they tend to distribute exceptionally high dividends to shareholders. Based on Tan Sri’s track record over the years, do you think he leans more towards being generous or frugal?

body:
RCE Capital’s latest quarterly results have delivered a highly positive signal: the company has ended a streak of seven consecutive quarters of year-on-year earnings decline and is officially back on a growth path.
Over previous quarters, RCE's profitability was under pressure due to increased impairment allowances resulting from a higher attrition rate among civil servants. The rebound in profit this quarter suggests that the worst of these headwinds may now be behind the company.
Dividend & Yield Outlook : Dividend Declared: First interim dividend of 3.0 sen. Ex-Date: December 16, 2025. Yield Estimation: Assuming a full-year payout of 6.0 – 10.0 sen (historically paid in two tranches, occasionally with special dividends) and based on the current share price of approximately RM 1.2 the estimated dividend yield is between 5% – 6%.
Key Catalyst: Civil Service Salary Hike Upcoming Adjustment: The Malaysian government has announced a salary increment for civil servants. Timeline: Expected to take formal effect in January 2026 (partial adjustment). Impact: As RCE Capital’s core business revolves around civil servant financing, this salary hike is expected to improve borrower credit quality and loan eligibility, serving as a significant tailwind for the company moving forward.
Take note :the price has just broken above the MA200, signaling a trend reversal to bullish. This is the first time this year, and it’s a strong bullish indicator.
Major Shareholder Action: A Strong Vote of Confidence Tan Sri Azman Bin Hashim’s Accumulation The continuous buying by Tan Sri Azman Bin Hashim (via his investment vehicle, Cempaka Empayar Sdn Bhd) is a significant market signal. His stake is now approaching the 60% threshold, indicating a high level of conviction in the company’s prospects.

title: After some consideration, Ah Tai has confirmed the need for USD 55 billion to develop the New York casino. Where will Ah Tai find this amount? Recently,
body:
After some consideration, Ah Tai has confirmed the need for USD 55 billion to develop the New York casino. Where will Ah Tai find this amount? Recently, Genting has been issuing bonds to borrow money for the acquisition of Genting Malaysia, and Genting Singapore is also undergoing a major renovation that requires substantial funding.
The most likely option is to prepare for an initial public offering (IPO) in the United States (similar to how Genting Singapore is listed on the Singapore Stock Exchange). Once listed, there will be a significant influx of US dollars to fund operations in the United States, and borrowing will become easier. The parent company, Genting, also owns an LVS casino in the United States. The current challenge is to first privatize Jack Ma's Genting Malaysia, as Genting Malaysia holds assets in the United States.

title: The Story of the Twin Giants of Genting～
author: jackyling
body:
The Story of the Twin Giants of Genting～
1) Why do many holdouts refuse to agree to the acquisition price of 2.35?
~26% of shareholders previously purchased too many tickets at inflated prices (trapped in high-cost speculation) and are now, out of stubbornness, still waiting for A-Tai to offer another inflated price. (No right or wrong, consequences are borne by themselves.)
2) What is the outlook for GENTING and GENM?
～GENM will delist once it reaches 75% ownership (Genting has already clearly stated this in its initial announcement). Do you think the remaining days will be easy?
~GENTING initially announced the acquisition and borrowing to build a casino in the United States. The acquisition is inevitable and must proceed. However, borrowing for such purposes also comes with a cost: *the aim is to ensure the stock price continues to rise steadily; otherwise, as you know, a margin call would be unpleasant.*
3) The market has been touting that GENM is undervalued, but why doesn't anyone say that GENTING is the real centerpiece of the entire story?
4) Of course, the above is just casual talk. Personally, I find the story fascinating and am very much looking forward to subsequent developments ✅

title: In-depth Analysis of the GENM Acquisition Battle The acquisition battle for GENM began the moment Genting announced its intention to acquire GENM. The business
author: 心如紫水
body: In-depth Analysis of the GENM Acquisition Battle The acquisition battle for GENM began the moment Genting announced its intention to acquire GENM. The business arena is akin to a battlefield, and as Sun Tzu's Art of War states: 'Know yourself and know your enemy, and you will win a hundred battles out of a hundred.' It is crucial to have a clear understanding of one’s own strength as well as that of the opponent. If Genting is the acquiring party, or the attacking side, then the minority shareholders of GENM are the defending side. This war has only one objective: GENM. Let us first list the cards each side holds: Attacking Party: Genting Group Commander: TS Lim Khoon Tai Resources: Cash of 6 billion, Genting Group assets exceeding 100 billion, top-tier advisors Morale: High, with a strong determination to succeed, having already secured a majority stake. Defending party: Minority shareholders of GENM. Commander-in-chief: Lack of leadership Resources: None, power is scattered, many self-proclaimed strategists and gurus Morale: Low, Stubborn The attacking party needs to capture two key thresholds to secure GENM: the 75% threshold and the 90% threshold. Crossing the 75% mark allows for the application of a trading halt, freezing all external support to corner the remaining shareholders. Crossing the 90% mark enables the company to apply for delisting, granting majority shareholders nearly unrestricted control, effectively securing victory. To secure 75% is actually not a difficult task. Everyone can refer to my previous analysis:https://www.facebook.com/groups This 75% is a confident estimate, but what about the remaining 25%? That’s hard to say, given that the offer price isn’t particularly high. As for how to reach the 90% threshold, capturing the leader first is key; this depends on who the main commander is. Commander: TS Lim Kok Thay, known for being meticulous and prudent in his approach, yet not hasty—this is evident to all. Given the commander's personality, shareholders should not expect any leniency or adjustments in the share price. Moreover, the commander is patient and unwilling to compromise, preferring to use a strategy of trading time for space to gradually acquire minority shareholders. Therefore, he can continuously employ tactics with frequent success. On the advisory side, besides having a highly professional Zhuge Liang-like strategist, there is also a team of traders calculating votes, and they can consult other financial tycoons for advice at any time. So what options do minority shareholders have? Looking at the situation of these small shareholders, they are essentially a group of retail investors. Major investors and funds have long withdrawn their support, as the funds see that the siege has already been completed, making it impossible for them to get involved. The best strategy out of the thirty-six stratagems is to retreat. As for major investors? Many of them are long-term shareholders who care only about receiving dividends; they are indifferent to acquisition battles, defensive strategies, or resistance efforts. In short, as long as they can collect money, they will remain content. In terms of advisors, there are only a group of amateur strategists, with the worst part being the presence of many unprofessional 'Gurus' (definitely not Tian Ge), and the resources available to them are extremely limited—lacking both networks and assets. To make matters worse, they act independently, resulting in differing opinions and ideas every day. In this confrontation, one side is a professional army, while the other can be considered an irregular force. It goes without saying who will emerge victorious. Since the acquirer is unwilling to raise the price, they will need to think of operational maneuvers instead. What kind of moves? Based on past examples and the commander’s personality, it will likely involve a slow grind. Since it involves a slow grind, the acquirer will ensure that the acquisition does not exceed 75%, as exceeding that would mean game over and necessitate an official declaration. By keeping the acquisition below 75%, additional efforts can be made to show that the ownership has surpassed 73%, leaving just 1% short. This creates a Sword of Damocles hanging over each minority shareholder, putting them in a dilemma. Every day, they fear that the company might cross the 75% threshold, leading to a potential trading halt. Once trading halts, who will buy or sell shares? This is just the beginning. Don’t forget, the company has already announced the failure of the acquisition, but it’s only short by 1%. Consequently, market liquidity will significantly decrease, as no fund would want to purchase shares of a company nearing delisting or with such poor liquidity. In other words, currently, very few people are buying GENM shares, and those wanting to sell can only wait for the sole buyer to make a move. Yes, this is essentially a trading halt without an official suspension, but with an added disadvantage: after a suspension or delisting, the final trading price becomes the reference for transactions, fixing the price for buying and selling based on the last traded price. However, without an official suspension, the price can fluctuate freely each day, potentially falling like a free-falling object due to a lack of buyers supporting the stock price. The share price can slide from 2.35 to 2.25, then to 2.15, 2.05, 1.9, 1.8, 1.7, and so on, until one day you can’t bear it anymore and let go. Understand this: I’m not trying to scare anyone. The gap to that 1% won’t be far, so don’t expect funds or major shareholders to step in and sweep up shares—it’s highly unrealistic. If this situation persists over time, floating shares in the market will gradually flow toward the Genting Group, ensuring the acquirer's victory. Once the 90% threshold is crossed, the acquirer can apply for delisting and mandatory redemption, thereby completing the privatization. The timeline doesn’t matter; the commander’s personality dictates patience, and he is willing to wait indefinitely. What twists and turns might occur, or what new tactics the acquirer may deploy, remain to be seen. However, as the defending side, they can only endure the blows. Don't ask me for ways to turn defeat into victory. There is an English saying: 'Those that care don't know, those that know don't care.' #Repost

title: Why did Lim Kok Thay increase his stake from 66.16% to 73.15% on the last day without directly reaching 75%? And why is he continuing to slowly purchase shares
author: 心如紫水
body: Why did Lim Kok Thay increase his stake from 66.16% to 73.15% on the last day without directly reaching 75%? And why is he continuing to slowly purchase shares in the market? He wants the market to face reality! Earlier, when he offered a price of 2.35, many people complained that it was too low, even demanding 2.6, 2.8, or 3. Yet, he managed to buy shares in the open market at 2.18, with prices dropping as low as 2.15. Now, the share price is only around 2.2. He is doing this to make the market realize that while dreams may be beautiful, reality can be harsh. Those who refused to sell at 2.35—would they reconsider selling if another offer of 2.35 were made now? Many didn’t sell earlier and even bought more at the bottom because the stake was only at 60% then, with one week left and many believing there was still room to fight. What happened in the end? On Friday, the stake was 66.16%, but on Monday, the last day before the deadline, it suddenly jumped to 73.13%! He is sending a message to the market: he still has ammunition! The idea of acquiring Genting Malaysia (Genm) did not just emerge in recent months; it was planned and strategically laid out several years ago. The current drop in share price to such a low level is no coincidence. How much of the opposing retail shareholders' camp might still belong to him and remain unsold? Unknown? Previously, when Genm’s stock dropped to a low of 1.46 and then rebounded from the bottom, who do you think was behind those purchases? Many believe that Lim Kok Thay's ultimate goal is to acquire up to 90% of the shares and then apply for a mandatory general offer. But I don’t think so. What he wants is simply that “as long as the opposition doesn’t exceed 10%, it’s considered approved!” Voter turnout is never 100%; participation above 95% is already considered very high. Some people feel their votes are insignificant and abstain, some forget to vote, others are confused, and some are “ghost shareholders” who remain completely inactive like ownerless spirits? If you don't oppose at the shareholders' meeting, your silence will be taken as consent! Once he reaches 75% control while public float remains below 25%, he can apply for a trading suspension. Typically, Bursa would give the company time to adjust its equity, but he won't need to! Earlier, Genting already stated that “once the acquisition reaches 75%, there is no intention to maintain the listing status,” meaning he might keep the stock suspended indefinitely. Suspension is not the same as delisting. If the shareholders’ meeting votes against the resolution, will Genm resume trading? It’s highly unlikely, as they have already stated they have no intention of maintaining the listing status. If they wanted to resume trading, they would need to sell down their holdings to below 75%. In my view, this is like meat buns thrown to dogs—there’s no turning back! Lim Kok Thay is likely to keep the stock suspended until the next offer. Retail investors won’t be able to sell, and no one will escape. During the suspension, they can only privately seek buyers themselves. If it fails the first time, the suspension could trap you for a year or more. Will you still have the same defiance the second time? What about the third or fourth attempt? Lim Kok Thay has plenty of strategies—he’ll use whichever suits him best! ... To be continued! #Repost

author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Key Takeaways:
• U.S. Stocks Edge Higher on Softer PCE and Big Tech Gains
• KLCI Eases on Caution Ahead of BOJ and US Data
• M-REITs Face Uncertainty Over Withholding Tax Concession
• Stocks to watch: MISC Bhd, Bintai Kinden, etc.
🇺🇸Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 6,870.40 (+0.19%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 47,954.99 (+0.22%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 23,578.13 (+0.31%)
U.S. stocks inched higher Friday as a cooler inflation print and a rebound in select Big Tech outweighed fresh crypto weakness. $纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ rose 0.3% to 23,578.13, the $道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ added 0.2% to 47,954.99, and the $标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ gained 0.2% to 6,870.40. The S&P and Nasdaq have now advanced four straight sessions; the Dow is up in three of the past four.
Big Tech leaders paced the move: $SanDisk Corp (SNDK.US)$ +7.1%, $Salesforce (CRM.US)$ +5.3%, $Micron Technology (MU.US)$ +4.7%, $CoreWeave (CRWV.US)$ +3.0%, $Broadcom (AVGO.US)$ +2.4%, $Intel (INTC.US)$ +2.3%, $Palantir (PLTR.US)$ +2.2%, and $Meta Platforms (META.US)$ +1.8%.
Crypto slid: $Bitcoin (BTC.CC)$ −3.2% to $89,323.86; $Ethereum (ETH.CC)$ −3.5% to $3,023.11; $Solana (SOL.CC)$ −7.4% to $132.58; $Ripple (XRP.CC)$ −3.4% to $2.03.
Core PCE—the Fed's preferred inflation gauge—came in at 2.8% for September after a shutdown delay, below the 2.9% forecast but still above the 2% target. The softer print lifted odds of a quarter‑point cut after Wednesday’s meeting to about 87% (vs. 62% a month ago), per CME FedWatch.
🇲🇾Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1,616.52 (-0.28%)
Top Gainer: $GAMUDA (5398.MY)$ RM5.24 (+1.75%)
Top Loser: $AXIATA (6888.MY)$ RM2.52 (-5.97%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.1171 (+0.13%)
Malaysian equities ended softer on Friday, mirroring a mixed performance across the region as investors turned cautious ahead of a possible Bank of Japan rate increase and US data that could influence the Federal Reserve's decision next week.
At the 5 pm close, the $富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ slipped 4.55 points, or 0.28%, to 1,616.52, having recovered from steeper intraday declines. The index opened slightly lower at 1,620.70 and fluctuated between 1,609.67 and 1,621.25.
Market breadth was weak, with 604 losers topping 439 gainers; 550 counters were unchanged, 1,151 saw no trades, and 18 were suspended. Turnover thinned to 3.17 billion shares valued at RM2.24 billion, down from 4.48 billion shares worth RM2.75 billion on Thursday.
Rakuten Trade's vice-president of equity research, Thong Pak Leng, expects the FBM KLCI to trade sideways in a 1,600–1,630 band this week as investors await fresh catalysts at home and abroad. With sturdy support around 1,600 and few immediate drivers, he sees range-bound action fostering further consolidation.
Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia's hardcore poverty rate has fallen to 0.09%, positioning the country close to eliminating it entirely. He aims to resolve remaining cases by the first quarter of 2026, crediting people-focused Madani initiatives—such as Adopted Village, Adopted School, and SejaTi Madani—backed by strong inter-agency coordination.
Malaysia's REIT sector risks a policy overhang as the 10% withholding tax on distributions to individuals and non-residents is set to expire on Dec 31, 2025, with no extension confirmed. If it lapses, investors would revert to marginal tax rates, potentially cutting post-tax yields by 50–100 bps and undermining competitiveness versus Singapore and Thailand—possibly prompting foreign outflows.
Maybank IB still expects renewal for YA 2026 but urges prompt MOF guidance for tax planning. The MRMA is lobbying for continuation, as prolonged uncertainty could pressure sentiment despite stable sector fundamentals.

$BINTAI (6998.MY)$ is suing vendor Yeo Eng Lam in the Melaka High Court to claim RM9.1 million under the profit guarantee for its 2021 purchase of Johnson Medical International.
Newly listed $GEOHAN (5345.MY)$ won two Penang LRT Mutiara Line contracts worth RM59 million from SRS LRT, covering bored piling works under sub‑packages BP01 (RM31.2 million) and BP02 (RM27.8 million).
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ launched a new unrated RM5 billion MTN programme, with the first series to partly fund its takeover offer for Genting Malaysia. Separately, Genting RMTN issued a RM1.35 billion eighth tranche under its existing RM10 billion MTCN programme.
$ANCOMNY (4758.MY)$ will sell 25% of new unit Maxlive to Thailand’s TOPNEXT for US$9.32 million (RM38.3 million) now, with an option for another 25% at the same price within five years, totaling about RM77 million.
$QUALITY (7544.MY)$ won a RM294.6 million contract from the Sarawak Rural Water Supply Department to build and upgrade the Mukah water supply system, a 30‑month job starting January 2026.
$HKB (0359.MY)$ landed a RM42.8 million contract from Jaya GC to build an immigration post and staff quarters in Serikin, Bau, Sarawak. The 24‑month project starts this month and is expected to boost FY2026 results.

author: Moomoo News MY
body:
In a week marked by cooling inflation and weak jobs data, global investors showed renewed appetite for Asian equities, snapping a four-week selling streak. The shift signals a sentiment lift amid economic uncertainties—let’s break down the moves.
Market Pulse
U.S. private-sector hiring slumped by 32k in November, while core PCE inflation held at +0.2% mom, fueling hopes for rate cuts. Consumer sentiment edged up but remained historically weak. Globally, 17 of 20 major indices rose, led by South Korea’s KOSPI (+4.42%) and Vietnam’s Ho Chi Minh VSE (+2.98%). The dollar dipped -0.53% against the Ringgit, and oil prices climbed. Despite patchy data, risk appetite perked up!
Asia’s Money Moves
Foreign investors poured USD1.45b into Asian equities, reversing four weeks of outflows. South Korea (USD1.14b), Vietnam (USD167.4m), Indonesia (USD149.4m), and Thailand (USD113.5m) led inflows, driven by solid GDP growth and trade surpluses. Only India (-USD1.32b) and the Philippines (-USD82.2m) saw outflows, amid rate cuts and inflation concerns. Asia’s appeal is back!
Malaysia Breakdown
Foreign investors turned net buyers on Bursa Malaysia after two weeks of selling, with a net inflow of RM11.6m. Local institutions continued buying (RM83.0m), but retailers turned sellers (-RM94.6m). Average daily trading volume fell across all investor groups: foreign investors (-28.8%), local institutions (-20.6%), and retailers (-3.3%). The financial sector led foreign inflows (RM532.0m), while utilities saw the largest outflows (-RM351.9m).

title: Foreign investors net bought Malaysian stocks worth MYR 11.6 million last week.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, August 8) Foreign investors ended two consecutive weeks of net selling, turning slightly net buyers of Malaysian stocks last week with net purchases amounting to MYR 11.6 million, compared to net sales of MYR 484.8 million the week before. Year-to-date, foreign capital outflows from Malaysia have totaled MYR 20.26 billion, significantly higher than the full-year net outflow of MYR 4.21 billion recorded last year. According to the latest fund flow report by Malacca Securities, foreign investors turned net sellers of Malaysian stocks again last Thursday and Friday, offloading MYR 80.3 million and MYR 172.3 million respectively. However, due to continuous inflows in the first three trading sessions, last week as a whole still saw net inflows. The sectors most favored by foreign investors last week were financial services (MYR 532 million), industrial products and services (MYR 83 million), and communications and media (MYR 58.6 million). Meanwhile, the sectors most heavily sold by foreign investors were utilities (-MYR 351.9 million), healthcare (-MYR 108.1 million), and technology (-MYR 86.7 million). On the other hand, local institutional investors were net buyers of Malaysian stocks last week, purchasing MYR 83 million worth, marking the second consecutive week of providing support to the market; however, retail investors turned to net selling, offloading MYR 94.6 million worth of Malaysian stocks last week. The average daily trading volume in the market last week generally declined, with trading activities of retail investors, local institutions, and foreign capital decreasing by 3.3%, 20.6%, and 28.8% respectively.

Now you can finally test the urban legend that Genting stocks rise just before the Lunar New Year... Those who previously sold GENM, 4715 at 2.34-2.35 have finally waited for the opportunity to enter and exchange shares.

Target price ~3.45. Regardless of whether you buy at 2.98~3.05-3.10 *10 lots, earning one free share is the objective of this trade.

title: Slower profit recovery and rising debt risks lead Moody's to downgrade Genting's rating.
author: 南洋商报 NYSP
body:
(Kuala Lumpur, 9th news) International rating agency Moody's downgraded Genting $GENTING (3182.MY)$ and its two subsidiaries—Genting Overseas Holdings and Genting Singapore. Moody's released the latest ratings while Genting was attempting to privatize Genting Malaysia through debt financing. $GENM (4715.MY)$at this time. According to Moody's statement, the ratings of Genting and Genting Overseas Holdings will be downgraded from Baa2 to Baa3, while the rating for Genting Singapore will be lowered from A3 to Baa1. The outlook for all three remains 'stable'. The agency noted: 'The downgrade of Genting’s ratings is mainly due to slower-than-expected profit recovery, prolonged constraints in deleveraging efforts, already weak financial conditions, and the additional financial burden from acquiring Genting Malaysia through debt financing. Moreover, further capital investment may still be required for the development of Resorts World New York, which will exacerbate financial pressures.' 'However, the stable outlook reflects our expectation that profitability in Singapore and Las Vegas will continue to improve, execution risks for the New York project remain manageable, and it is expected to start contributing profits by the second half of 2026, thereby improving the group’s credit metrics.' Moody's added that Genting’s standalone liquidity position remains robust, primarily supported by fees and dividends from its operating subsidiaries. Heavy debt pressure in 2027 However, Genting will face the pressure of debt maturity in 2027, including a USD 1.5 billion (approximately MYR 6.16 billion) note issued by Genting Overseas Holdings Capital, which is due in January 2027. Subsequently, a total of MYR 1.9 billion in debt from its subsidiaries, Genting RMTN Corporation and Genting Capital Corporation, will mature in March and June 2027, respectively. We expect Genting to refinance at least part of its upcoming maturing debt within the next 6 to 12 months. Last week, CreditSights, a credit research firm under Fitch, also warned that both Genting and Genting Malaysia face the risk of rating downgrades due to their high debt levels and pressured cash flows. Previously, Moody's had placed Genting on its rating watch list in October, pending the outcome of the full acquisition of Genting Malaysia. As of early December, Genting’s privatization offer has expired, during which it acquired 73.133% of Genting Malaysia’s shares, but the privatization was unsuccessful.
