title: The father worked tirelessly to turn a barren mountain into a gold mine, but the son turned that gold mine into a mountain of debt! The saddest part is that
author: 韭菜炒雞蛋
body:
The father worked tirelessly to turn a barren mountain into a gold mine, but the son turned that gold mine into a mountain of debt! The saddest part is that shareholders are ultimately forced to foot the bill to clean up the mess!
Lim Goh Tong spent his entire life building the Genting empire. After Lim Kok Thay took over, he had grand ambitions to conquer the world. As a result, while the business expanded, so did the debt, with the group's borrowings now reaching RM45.2 billion!
Massive bets in Las Vegas yielded disappointing returns. Now, they are preparing to raise another RM1.25 billion from shareholders.
When investments succeed, the boss takes the credit; when they fail, the bill is sent to shareholders?
In the past, gamblers went to Genting to lose money; now, even shareholders who buy Genting stock are being asked to dig into their pockets!
Lim Goh Tong left behind a gold mine, but Lim Kok Thay has left shareholders with one bill after another.
The most ironic part is that gamblers can walk away after losing, but shareholders who suffer losses are actually called back to inject more capital!

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | Malaysia Budget 2027 Sets Policy Tone

body:
📌 Key Takeaways
• US stocks rose as investors reversed AI-led selling; S&P 500 +0.59%
• Oil eased 0.5% to $91.04 after Russia diesel deal announcement
• KLCI gained 0.46% as Budget 2027 outlined 4.2%-5.2% GDP growth
• Moderna jumped 14.2% at close; Palantir hit record $209.05 close
• Stocks to Watch: TENAGA, IOIPG, etc.
🇺🇸 Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 7,811.54(+0.59%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 51,654.95(+0.83%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 27,366.17(+0.64%)
U.S. stocks rebounded on Friday as investors judged Thursday's AI-driven sell-off excessive. The $道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ rose 423.31 points (0.83%) to 51,654.95, the $纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ gained 172.83 points (0.64%) to 27,366.17, and the $标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ added 46.18 points (0.59%) to 7,811.54. Sentiment improved after the prior-day retreat tied to a Financial Times report that OpenAI generates about $50 billion in annual revenue, below previously published figures and raising concerns over AI buildout spending. Oil also eased after President Donald Trump announced a deal allowing Russia to sell some diesel fuel to the U.S. and other countries; $WTI原油期货主连 (2611) (CLmain.US)$ slipped 0.5% to $91.04.
Among gainers, $Moderna (MRNA.US)$ jumped 14.2% in its first session as a Nasdaq-100 member and on a report that the U.S. National Institutes of Health are launching a public/private partnership to promote anti-cancer vaccines. $Palantir (PLTR.US)$ climbed 5.2% to a record $209.05 close after Barclays initiated coverage with an Overweight rating and a $265 price target, while $Lumentum (LITE.US)$ rose 5.2% after its CEO told Bloomberg TV components are essentially sold out through early 2029. In Big Tech, $甲骨文 (ORCL.US)$ gained 4.6%, $亚马逊 (AMZN.US)$ rose 3.3%, $微软 (MSFT.US)$ added 2.4% and $特斯拉 (TSLA.US)$ advanced 2.1%, while telecom names slumped on Starlink competition fears, led by $T-Mobile US (TMUS.US)$, down 13.3%.
🇲🇾 Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1608.450(+0.46%)
Top Gainer: $99SMART (5326.MY)$ RM3.230 (+3.53%)
Top Loser: $PETGAS (6033.MY)$ RM17.120 (-3.82%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.0857(-0.15%)
The $富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ rose 7.35 points, or 0.46%, to 1,608.45 in the previous session, with $99SMART (5326.MY)$ leading gainers at RM3.230 (+3.53%) while $PETGAS (6033.MY)$ was the top loser at RM17.120 (-3.82%). The $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ stood at 4.0857, down 0.15%.
Malaysia's 2027 Economic Report projects GDP growth of 4.2%-5.2%, while inflation is expected to edge higher. The Fiscal Report also indicated a modest increase in development spending and a narrower fiscal deficit, setting the policy backdrop for today's market sentiment.
Budget 2027 allocated RM5.33 billion to PETRA to strengthen water and energy infrastructure, alongside incentives and investments tied to the energy transition. Separately, the government and Grab will fund a RM160 million package for e-hailing and p-hailing workers, while funding for biodiversity, wildlife and green technology was also increased under NRES.
🔍 IPO Scanner
🔔 Stocks to Watch
$TENAGA (5347.MY)$: Malaysia's 2027 Budget allocates RM15 billion to strengthen the national grid, with Tenaga Nasional saying the investment will support grid reliability and capacity upgrades. The measure is linked to national power infrastructure development and energy transition-related spending under the budget framework.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$: Genting plans a RM1.25 billion rights issue as part of efforts to pare down debt. The proposed capital raising is a balance sheet-related exercise and ranks among the day's larger financing developments involving a major Bursa Malaysia-listed group.
$IOIPG (5249.MY)$: IOI Properties Group said it is in talks for a potential secondary listing on the Singapore Exchange, according to its chief executive officer. The plan remains under discussion and represents a capital markets initiative aimed at broadening the group's market presence.
$UNISEM (5005.MY)$: Unisem plans to invest RM396 million to expand its advanced semiconductor packaging capacity. The expansion adds to Malaysia's semiconductor manufacturing pipeline and is tied to higher-end packaging capabilities within the group's operations.
$PMBTECH (7172.MY)$: PMB Technology plans a RM650 million silicon-aluminium alloy plant in Sarawak, marking an expansion into a new product segment. The proposed smelter project represents a major capital expenditure commitment and an increase in manufacturing capacity.
$AAGB (5238.MY)$: Astral Asia signed a pact to sell land in Pahang for RM233.6 million, following earlier reports that it was exploring a roughly RM234 million disposal. The transaction is an asset monetisation exercise and is expected to strengthen the company's cash position upon completion.
$PENERGY (5133.MY)$: Petra Energy is selling a work barge for RM18.4 million and said the disposal is expected to result in a gain of RM3.2 million. The vessel sale forms part of the company's asset rationalisation and has a direct identified impact on earnings through the disposal gain.

body:
To make matters worse, your ordeal is far from over. Since you hold approximately 25,250 shares (a significant portion of your assets is now trapped):

If you wait until the ex-rights date for the bonus shares in the first quarter of next year, once the exchange's computer system resets, your share price could be forcibly adjusted down to RM1.40 or even lower. If you do not participate in the rights issue, the losses in your account will passively expand, resulting in an immediate erosion of your asset value.

If you choose to subscribe by paying cash: Based on the projected 4-for-1 ratio, you must inject an additional approximately RM7,500 in cash between January and March next year to subscribe for new shares, thereby preventing your equity stake from being diluted.

This presents a dire dilemma: whether to 'cut off one's arm to survive' (take a painful loss to exit) or 'keep throwing money into a bottomless pit' (continue investing to cover losses).

U.S. stocks ended mixed on Monday as a pullback in technology shares and firmer oil prices weighed on sentiment. The $纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ fell 120.27 points, or 0.4%, to 27,245.90, while the $标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ slipped 4.30 points, or 0.1%, to 7,807.24. In contrast, the $道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ added 195.60 points, or 0.4%, to 51,850.55. Higher energy prices also added pressure after a Houthi attack on a Saudi civilian airport and after Ukraine said Russia had broken a weekend energy-infrastructure deal. $WTI原油期货主连 (2611) (CLmain.US)$ rose 1.5% to $93.25 a barrel.
Technology names led the downside. $Cerebras Systems (CBRS.US)$ dropped 10.7%, $Lumentum (LITE.US)$ lost 9.8%, and $IonQ Inc (IONQ.US)$ fell 9.1%. Optical peers $Applied Optoelectronics (AAOI.US)$ and $Coherent (COHR.US)$ declined 8.2% and 7.9%, respectively. Memory and AI-linked stocks also retreated, with $美光科技 (MU.US)$ down 3.9%, $英特尔 (INTC.US)$ off 3.2%, $美国超微公司 (AMD.US)$ down 2.3%, $英伟达 (NVDA.US)$ losing 1.3%, and $特斯拉 (TSLA.US)$ shedding 1.2%.
Among gainers, $Meta Platforms (META.US)$ rallied 3.4% after unveiling its Muse Wonder AI agent. Other advances included $赛富时 (CRM.US)$, up 2.1%, $苹果 (AAPL.US)$, up 1.3%, and $耐克 (NKE.US)$, up 1.8%.

Malaysia's government is in discussions with Tenaga Nasional and the energy regulator on electricity subsidy measures for 2027, keeping focus on utility pricing, fiscal outlays and inflation transmission. Separately, UOB said gross government borrowings could ease to MYR180 billion in 2027, while CIMB noted the absence of external debt maturities next year may provide more flexibility in funding plans.
In commodities, Malaysia's September palm oil inventory rose 24.5% month on month as production increased and exports declined, a key data point for the plantation sector. Analysts also said a minimum wage hike could lift labour costs for plantation companies, while oil prices fell on expectations a Russia-Ukraine energy ceasefire could increase supply.

$GENTING (3182.MY)$ and $GENM (4715.MY)$ remained in focus after the group announced a cash call of more than RM1 billion, while Bursa Malaysia suspended intraday short selling for Genting Malaysia shares and separately halted intraday short selling in Genting after the counter hit the exchange's trigger level. The developments were regulatory and funding-related measures tied to recent trading conditions.
$MNHLDG (0245.MY)$ won a RM294 million contract to develop power infrastructure facilities for a data centre. The contract adds a sizeable data centre-linked job to the group's pipeline and underscores continued project flow in utility works tied to digital infrastructure.
$IOIPG (5249.MY)$ is looking to acquire a 50% stake in One Raffles Place in Singapore. The proposed transaction would give the group exposure to a prime commercial asset in Singapore's central business district, subject to the finalisation of deal terms and approvals.
$MASTEEL (5098.MY)$ plans to acquire a 51% stake in a power infrastructure company for RM12 million. The proposed acquisition would expand the steelmaker's presence into power infrastructure-related activities as part of its business diversification efforts.
$SWIFT (5303.MY)$, via Swift Energy Technology, secured RM59.1 million in orders involving data centres and gas projects. The newly secured jobs strengthen near-term order visibility across engineering works tied to energy and industrial infrastructure.
$INFOM (0265.MY)$ renewed a RM22.1 million contract with Panasonic Digital. The renewal extends the Malaysian technology firm's service engagement with the Japanese client and supports recurring revenue from its software and IT services business.

body: https://youtu.be/7Mx1GOyFU2w?si=176ArZkZCUx50CYR Analysts vs. Rating Agencies: The Truth Behind Genting’s Rights Issue @YZFinanceMY Genting Berhad at a Strategic Crossroads: Balancing Equity Concerns and Balance Sheet Stability Genting Berhad’s proposed RM1.25 billion rights issue highlights the delicate balance between maintaining shareholder equity and protecting credit ratings. The market’s reaction reflects two starkly contrasting perspectives: 1️⃣ Equity Analysts: Expressing concern over potential share dilution and negative market signaling. 2️⃣ Credit Rating Agencies: Supporting the initiative as a necessary step toward debt reduction and balance sheet stabilization. The Financial Pressures Driving the Decision: • Leveraged Share Acquisition: In late 2025, Genting expanded its stake in Genting Malaysia to nearly 74% via a RM3.3 billion purchase, funded primarily through short-term borrowings. • Dividend Constraints: Cash distribution from Genting Malaysia diminished as capital was diverted toward Resorts World New York City’s expansion. • Maturity Wall: As of mid-2026, Genting faces RM9.7 billion in short-term debt obligations, with narrowed long-term refinancing options following credit downgrades. • Capital Drag: Projects like Kasuri LNG continue to consume capital without generating cash flow, while Resorts World Las Vegas remains loss-making due to high financing costs despite strong EBITDA. The Strategic Imperative: Capital Recycling A broader governance issue lies in Genting's attachment to non-performing "strategic assets" (e.g., idle Miami land, PUC shares, and the Bintan casino project via Landmarks). While core operations (Resorts World Genting, Resorts World Sentosa, and Resorts World New York City) remain solid profit drivers, underperforming overseas properties continue to drain capital. To rebuild long-term balance sheet strength, analysts argue that Genting must transition toward disciplined capital recycling—divesting non-core holdings and monetizing idle assets. How can conglomerate boards better execute capital recycling during debt squeezes? Share your thoughts in the comments below. https://youtu.be/7Mx1GOyFU2w?si=176ArZkZCUx50CYR #CorporateStrategy #FinancialRestructuring #Genting #CapitalMarkets #BalanceSheetManagement #Leadership Genting Group at a Strategic Crossroads: Weighing Equity Dilution Against Balance Sheet Stability The MYR 1.25 billion rights issue proposed by Genting Berhad highlights the dilemma companies face in balancing shareholder value preservation with maintaining credit ratings. Capital markets have reacted with two sharply divergent viewpoints: 1️⃣ Equity Analysts: Concerned about equity dilution and the negative signal sent to the market. 2️⃣ Credit Rating Agencies: Express support, viewing it as a viable move to reduce debt and stabilize the balance sheet. Key Financial Drivers Behind the Move: • Leveraged Stake Increase: By the end of 2025, Genting relied primarily on short-term borrowing to raise MYR 3.3 billion, boosting its stake in Genting Malaysia to nearly 74%. • Constrained Dividend Repatriation: Genting Malaysia has reduced dividend payouts to its parent company as capital is being directed toward the expansion of Resorts World New York City. • Mounting Short-Term Debt Pressure: By mid-2026, Genting faces MYR 9.7 billion in maturing short-term debt, while long-term refinancing channels have narrowed following a credit rating downgrade. • Capital-draining items: The Kasuri LNG project continues to consume capital without generating cash flow, while Resorts World Las Vegas, despite strong EBITDA, remains loss-making due to high financing costs. Strategic transformation is imminent: Rebalancing the asset portfolio Beyond debt pressure, Genting’s long-term retention of “strategic assets” (such as idle land in Miami, PUC shares, and Landmarks equity held for the Bintan Island casino project) has become a burden during periods of tight liquidity. While Resorts World Genting, Resorts World Singapore, and Resorts World New York continue to serve as strong profit engines, projects in Las Vegas, the Catskills, Bimini, and Birmingham have failed to deliver commensurate investment returns. Analysts point out that if Genting is to revitalize its balance sheet and restore market confidence, it must adopt a rigorous “capital recovery” strategy—monetizing idle assets, divesting non-core businesses, and concentrating resources on high-return, quality projects. body: https://youtu.be/fS-SAzICncY?si=x--84cm1-abaiNav Why Markets Love Expansion-Focused Rights Issues But Hate Debt Repayment @YZFinanceMY Not all rights issues are created equal! 💡 When companies announce a rights issue, investor reaction usually hinges on one crucial factor: where is the money going? 📈 Expansion-Driven: Markets welcome capital raises aimed at growth. For example, Axiata’s 2019 rights issue funded its digital expansion, and Sime Darby Plantation’s 2017 exercise backed strategic restructuring. Shareholders supported both despite dilution because they promised future earnings. 📉 Deleveraging-Driven: When rights issues are purely for debt repayment, markets get skeptical. AirAsia X’s RM1.4 billion raise in 2015 was seen as a survival move, while Maybank’s RM6 billion raise in 2009 faced criticism over timing and dilution. ⚖️ The Genting Split: Genting’s RM1.25 billion rights issue highlights this gap perfectly—credit rating agencies love the reduced leverage, but equity analysts worry about EPS dilution without growth upside. Bottom Line: Markets reward capital raised for profitable growth, but remain wary of simple debt cleanup. https://youtu.be/fS-SAzICncY?si=x--84cm1-abaiNav #CorporateFinance #RightsIssue #Genting #Investing #StockMarket #CapitalRaising Not all rights issues are created equal! 💡 When a company announces a rights issue, investor reaction often hinges on one key factor: How will the funds be used? 📈 Business Expansion Driver: The market generally welcomes fundraising aimed at business growth. For instance, Axiata issued rights in 2019 to fund its digital business expansion, while Sime Darby Plantation used financing in 2017 to drive long-term strategic restructuring. Despite equity dilution, shareholders remained supportive as these projects promised future earnings growth. 📉 Deleveraging/Debt Repayment Driver: If a rights issue is purely for repaying debt, the market tends to be skeptical. AirAsia X's raise of RM 1.4 billion in 2015 was seen as a survival move, while Maybank's plan to raise RM 6 billion in 2009 faced criticism over timing and dilution concerns. ⚖️ Genting's Divided View: Genting's RM 1.25 billion rights issue epitomizes this divide—credit rating agencies welcomed the stabilization of its debt ratio, but equity analysts worried about dilution without clear growth potential. Core Conclusion: The market tends to reward financing that funds profitable growth, while remaining cautious about moves solely aimed at reducing financial leverage. https://youtu.be/fS-SAzICncY?si=x--84cm1-abaiNav #CorporateFinance #RightsIssue #Genting #StockInvestment #StockMarketNews #CapitalRaising

The actual long-term value impact will depend on the final rights ratio and pricing, the discount to TERP, and whether the debt repayment and interest savings are enough to offset the dilution to earnings and dividends. The current sharp decline in GENTING’s share price suggests the market is already pricing in near-term dilution and balance-sheet stress.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | Hotter US CPI Hits Tech; CRESS Revision Keeps Energy in Focus
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
📌 Key Takeaways
• US stocks fell as September CPI topped forecasts, lifting rate-hike odds
• Nasdaq slid 1.9% at close as tech weakened and oil rose
• KLCI gained 0.27% at close, led by MISC up 5.68%
• CRESS charge revised to 18 sen/kWh, affecting renewables and data centres
• Stocks to Watch: Informina, Genting,etc.
🇺🇸 Wall Street Summary
$标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ 7,718.94(-1.11%)
$道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ 51,621.48(-0.09%)
$纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ 26,692.87(-1.88%)
Wall Street closed lower on Wednesday as hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation, firmer oil prices and broad technology weakness pressured risk appetite. The $纳斯达克综合指数 (.IXIC.US)$ dropped 511.51 points, or 1.9%, to 26,692.87, while the $标普500指数 (.SPX.US)$ fell 86.51 points, or 1.1%, to 7,718.94 and the $道琼斯指数 (.DJI.US)$ slipped 48.62 points, or 0.1%, to 51,621.48. September CPI rose 3.7% year-on-year versus a 3.6% forecast, while core CPI came in at 2.6% against expectations for 2.5%. According to CME FedWatch, the odds of a 25-basis-point October rate hike rose to 32.7% from 17.7% a week ago. Meanwhile, $WTI原油期货主连 (2612) (CLmain.US)$ gained 1.0% to $95.09 a barrel.
Technology names led the retreat. $CoreWeave (CRWV.US)$ plunged 15.5% after Chamath Palihapitiya warned of a possible AI private-credit “bubble,” dragging $IREN Ltd (IREN.US)$ down 12.2% and $NEBIUS (NBIS.US)$ lower by 10.1%. $戴尔科技 (DELL.US)$ slumped 11.3% to $507.93 after a Barclays downgrade, while $IonQ Inc (IONQ.US)$ lost 9.5% following a $2 billion secondary offering. $阿斯麦 (ASML.US)$ fell 3.9% after revenue missed estimates. Among megacaps, $Meta Platforms (META.US)$, $英伟达 (NVDA.US)$ and $特斯拉 (TSLA.US)$ lost 3.3%, 3.2% and 2.2%, respectively, while only $苹果 (AAPL.US)$ rose, up 0.5%. Outside tech, $联合健康 (UNH.US)$ gained 4.7%, while $美国银行 (BAC.US)$ fell 4.8%.
🇲🇾 Bursa Market Insight
$富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ 1627.720(+0.27%)
Top Gainer: $MISC (3816.MY)$ RM8.370 (+5.68%)
Top Loser: $MAXIS (6012.MY)$ RM3.470 (-2.53%)
USD/MYR: $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.0825(-0.08%)
The $富时马来西亚指数 (.KLSE.MY)$ closed at 1,627.72, up 4.43 points or 0.27%, with $MISC (3816.MY)$ the top gainer at RM8.37 (+5.68%) and $MAXIS (6012.MY)$ the top loser at RM3.47 (-2.53%). USD/MYR stood at $美元/马来西亚令吉 (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.0825, down 0.08%.
Malaysia's energy and renewable-related sectors remain in focus after reports said the CRESS grid access charge was revised to 18 sen/kWh, marking a second change within a month. The reported adjustment has implications for renewable energy, power and data centre-related projects, while former energy minister Yeo Bee Yin has called for clarification on the reported reversal, citing potential implications for investor confidence and project planning.
Regionally, Singapore's central bank kept policy unchanged as easing inflation momentum supported its stance, while CIMB and UOB expect the MAS to remain on hold well into next year. Separately, HLIB maintained an overweight call on Malaysia's construction sector, reflecting continued attention on domestic infrastructure and execution trends.
🔍 IPO Scanner
🔔 Stocks to Watch
$IHH (5225.MY)$ is reportedly among bidders for TPG's Malaysian hospital assets, according to the headline. Separately, IHH associate Parkway Life REIT said it will acquire three nursing homes in France for $43.48 million, expanding its overseas asset base.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ said it will use RM280 million from the working capital portion of its rights issue proceeds to pay interest costs. The update reflects a change in the utilisation of funds raised, relating to the group's financing and debt-servicing arrangements.
$CAPITALA (5099.MY)$ was in focus after a Sabah MP called for government intervention over AirAsia's operational and financial difficulties, days after another MP cautioned Putrajaya against any bailout. The development centres on potential policy response and does not involve a corporate filing by the company.
$HIBISCS (5199.MY)$ signed a pact with developer Seri Pajam Development to explore energy solutions for data centres. The collaboration is aimed at studying power supply options for data centre-related developments and marks an expansion into a new use case for energy infrastructure.
$INFOM (0265.MY)$ reported stronger first-quarter earnings, with net profit rising 27%-31% year on year based on separate reports, supported by demand for IT infrastructure and technology support services. The company's quarterly update points to continued growth in its core enterprise technology business.
$AWC (7579.MY)$ secured a data centre-related subcontract worth about RM39.70 million to RM40 million for plumbing and sanitary works at a project in Port Dickson linked to Gamuda. The award adds to its order book through mechanical and engineering-related building services work.
$JAG (0024.MY)$ announced two expansion-related moves: the acquisition of industrial land in Shah Alam to grow its total waste management business, and a unit's agreement to buy a 6.17% stake in Australia's Metal Bank. The transactions represent asset deployment into domestic capacity expansion and an overseas strategic investment.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | Tech Sell-Off Drags Wall Street; Bursa Slips as Oil Climbs
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
📌 Key Takeaways
• US stocks fell as AI funding fears hit tech; Nasdaq -2.2% at close
• Bursa Malaysia dropped 0.98% at close as oil surged, tech volatility persisted
• Energy stocks rose with crude up 3.9% to $101.81 amid geopolitical tensions
• BNM kept Maybank, CIMB and Public Bank capital buffers unchanged
• Stocks to watch: Public Bank, Zetrix AI, etc.
🇺🇸 Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 7,659.44(-1.09%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 52,002.41(-0.34%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 26,140.03(-2.14%)
U.S. stocks ended sharply lower on Friday, led by a tech sell-off as investors questioned the sustainability of heavy AI-related capital spending. The $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ dropped 572.99 points (2.2%) to 26,140.03, while the $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ lost 84.62 points (1.1%) to 7,659.44 and the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ fell 175.28 points (0.3%) to 52,002.41. Sentiment was pressured by concerns after unsecured bonds tied to $CoreWeave (CRWV.US)$'s AI expansion reached 15% effective yields, raising worries over financing risks. Adding to the risk-off tone, $WTI原油期货主连 (2612) (CLmain.US)$ rose 3.9% to $101.81 a barrel amid Persian Gulf hostilities and signs a U.S.-led ceasefire on Russia-Ukraine energy infrastructure attacks is breaking down.
$CoreWeave (CRWV.US)$ slumped 11.9%, while AI-linked names including $NEBIUS (NBIS.US)$, $Applied Digital (APLD.US)$ and $IREN Ltd (IREN.US)$ fell 12.2%, 11.5% and 11.2%, respectively. Chip-related stocks also weakened, with $Advanced Micro Devices (AMD.US)$ down 6.0%, $Micron Technology (MU.US)$ off 5.6% and $Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US)$ lower by 2.3% despite record Q3 results and higher forward guidance. Among the Magnificent Seven, only $Apple (AAPL.US)$ rose, up 0.4%, while $Meta Platforms (META.US)$ fell 3.7% and $Tesla (TSLA.US)$ lost 2.1%.
Energy stocks outperformed, with $Occidental Petroleum (OXY.US)$ up 2.8%, $Chevron (CVX.US)$ gaining 2.6% and $Exxon Mobil (XOM.US)$ adding 2.5%. Crypto-related assets and stocks also retreated, with $Bitcoin (BTC.CC)$ down 1.0% and $Strategy (MSTR.US)$ falling 9.6%.
🇲🇾 Bursa Market Insight
$FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ 1607.760(-0.98%)
Top Gainer: $MISC (3816.MY)$ RM8.760 (+5.54%)
Top Loser: $PMETAL (8869.MY)$ RM6.500 (-9.34%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.0815(-0.08%)
Malaysian equities ended lower, with the $FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI Index (.KLSE.MY)$ closing at 1,607.760, down 15.93 points or 0.98%. $MISC (3816.MY)$ was the top gainer at RM8.760, up 5.54%, while $PMETAL (8869.MY)$ led decliners, falling 9.34% to RM6.500; $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ stood at 4.0815, down 0.08%.
Bank Negara Malaysia kept Malayan Banking, CIMB Bank and Public Bank on its domestic systemically important banks list, with additional Common Equity Tier 1 capital buffers unchanged. The decision maintains current regulatory capital requirements for Malaysia's three key banking groups.
Global market sentiment remains focused on higher oil prices, with crude reportedly reaching $110 a barrel, alongside renewed volatility in technology stocks. Separately, the Energy Commission fixed CRESS charges at 14 sen/kWh for developers and four sen/kWh for green consumers, while the government said six chips developed under the Semiconductor IC Design Park carry RM300 million in potential sales.
🔍 IPO Scanner
🔔 Stocks to Watch
$Public Bank (1295.MY)$: The bank said its Hong Kong unit will recognise a non-cash goodwill impairment of up to HK$1.964 billion. Public Bank said the write-off would reduce group net assets and earnings by about four sen per share.
$RHB Bank (1066.MY)$: The lender is seeking more time to complete its insurance merger with Tokio Marine. The development indicates the transaction has not yet been concluded and remains subject to further process and approvals.
$Tenaga Nasional (5347.MY)$: Power supply was restored within 77 minutes after a fire at the Kangkar Tebrau substation. In a separate incident, two Tenaga workers were injured in an electric shock case, marking another operational and workplace safety event involving the utility.
$Genting (3182.MY)$: Genting was in focus after a report said the group had lost some appeal, while a separate filing showed its chairman bought additional shares as the stock traded near a two-decade low. The latest disclosure points to insider share accumulation, though no transaction value was provided in the input.
$IOI Properties Group (5249.MY)$: The company said its board has yet to deliberate on potential acquisitions in Singapore. The statement indicates no decision has been made on the possible overseas assets at this stage.
$MSM Malaysia (5202.MY)$: MSM's sugar refinery lease in Prai will continue for another 15 years. The long-term lease extension supports the continuity of operations at the Prai facility over the medium to longer term.
$Zetrix AI (0138.MY)$: The company faces potential sukuk-related pressure after concerns emerged over obligations amounting to RM2.16 billion, while another report flagged breach risk after its founder ceased to be a major shareholder. The developments centre on financing covenants and possible implications for its sukuk structure.

title: According to the "One-Dollar Rule," every ringgit or dollar of cash retained by Genting's management should translate into incremental stock market value
author: 偶尔幸运
body:
According to the "One-Dollar Rule," every ringgit or dollar of cash retained by Genting's management should translate into incremental stock market value exceeding the market average in the future. Reviewing Genting management's capital allocation decisions from this perspective reveals significant contradictions and imbalances. Genting's management has long been committed to directing gaming cash flows into diversified expansion. The substantial retained earnings consumed in these high-risk areas failed to generate corresponding growth in free cash flow per share; instead, they significantly depressed the return on capital for both the parent company and its listed subsidiaries, resulting in a long period where the incremental market capitalization fell far short of total retained earnings.
There is a mismatch between high executive compensation and shareholder returns. In years when certain subsidiaries faced performance challenges or even recorded massive provisions, management's compensation and salaries remained at very high levels, while dividend policies for ordinary shareholders were relatively conservative. This incentive structure favors "empire building" over "maximizing per-share value," leading to significant agency costs.
If management had abandoned high-risk, aggressive cross-border expansion and non-core businesses, dedicating 100% of core cash flows to fortifying the deep moats in Singapore and Genting Highlands through continuous price increases and experience upgrades, and returning all remaining surplus to shareholders via dividends or share buybacks when undervalued, Genting could have become a highly defensive, high-dividend "cash bond." In such a scenario, the long-term total return created for shareholders (market cap growth + cumulative dividends) would have far exceeded actual performance.
However, reality did not unfold in this direction. Management chose to pursue scale and the construction of an international empire, causing the overall compound return to be dragged down by mediocre or even loss-making marginal assets, thereby diluting what were originally exceptional monopoly assets.

title: Foreign Funds Dump Utilities as Retail Investors Step In on Bursa Malaysia
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
Energy prices are back in the driver’s seat—and markets are feeling every bump. The latest MBSB Fund Flow Report shows inflation worries rising, global equities moving in different directions, and foreign investors staying cautious across much of Asia. In Malaysia, meanwhile, retail investors kept buying even as foreign and local institutions turned sellers.
Market Pulse：Global Economy at a Glance
Energy was the week’s big spoiler. US September headline CPI rose 3.7% year-on-year, while core inflation reached 2.6%. Producer prices were even hotter: headline PPI jumped 1.3% month-on-month and 6.3% year-on-year.
Consumers, however, were still spending. US retail sales rose 0.8% month-on-month, beating expectations, helped by higher gasoline spending. Markets reacted unevenly: FTSE 100 gained 3.1%, Sensex added 3.1%, and DAX 40 rose 2.1%, while the S&P 500 fell 2.0%, Nasdaq lost 4.5%, and Nikkei dropped 5.4%.
Brent crude climbed 4.9% to US$109.86 per barrel. The ringgit strengthened 0.1% against the US dollar to RM4.0810. Bottom line? Inflation fears are back, but risk appetite has not disappeared.
Asia’s Money Moves：Foreign Investors Stay Defensive
Across the eight Asian markets monitored, foreign investors extended their selling streak to three weeks, pulling out a combined US$28.32bn. Most markets recorded outflows, while Thailand was the sole market to attract foreign money, with net inflows of US$113.9m.
South Korea saw US$8.33bn in net outflows, its ninth consecutive week of selling, despite strong export-price and export-value growth. India recorded US$830.4m in outflows as inflation accelerated to 5.54%, driven by higher food, transport and restaurant prices.
Indonesia lost US$176.5m after MSCI proposed removing the country from its Emerging Markets Index, raising concerns over transparency and trading practices. Vietnam saw US$116.2m leave the market, even as trade negotiations with the US moved closer to completion.
Malaysia Breakdown：Retail Buys While Institutions Sell
Bursa Malaysia remained under foreign pressure in the week ended 16 October. Foreign institutions sold RM270.2m net, extending their selling streak to four consecutive weeks. They were net sellers on all five trading days, with Monday recording the largest outflow of RM105.7m, followed by Wednesday’s RM84.6m.
Local institutions also turned sellers, recording RM140.3m in net outflows after three straight weeks of net buying. Retail investors moved in the opposite direction. They extended their buying streak to eight weeks, accumulating RM410.5m net.
Trading activity was mixed. Retail average daily trading volume fell 13.4%, while local-institution and foreign-institution participation rose by 4.4% and 4.8%, respectively.
Foreign buying was focused on Financial Services, which attracted RM88.5m, followed by Healthcare at RM55.5m and Transportation & Logistics at RM52.8m. On the selling side, Utilities saw RM201.3m in outflows, followed by Industrial Products & Services at RM131.3m and Plantation at RM75.8m.

Strategy Breakdown: Who Is Playing What?
Local Institutions: Rotation Rather Than a Full Exit?
Local institutions were net sellers overall, but their buying of Tenaga Nasional, Malayan Banking and Sunway Construction points to selective positioning rather than a broad market retreat.
The pattern looks mixed. They added exposure to utilities, banks and construction, but reduced holdings in CIMB, Public Bank, Press Metal and UWC. This may reflect stock-specific rotation, though the report does not provide enough information to determine long-term holding intentions.
Local Retail: Buying Into Familiar Names
Retail investors continued to buy aggressively, favouring Press Metal, Malayan Banking, Genting-linked counters and YTL Power. This suggests continued interest in liquid, familiar names and active themes such as aluminium, banking and utilities.
At the same time, retail investors sold Top Glove and Public Bank. The behaviour shows a more tactical approach: investors were not simply buying the market, but rotating between individual stocks.
Foreign Investors: Banks In, Utilities Out
Foreign institutions were net sellers overall, yet they selectively accumulated Public Bank, CIMB and Top Glove. Their biggest exits were Tenaga Nasional and Malayan Banking.
This is a notable split. Foreign funds appeared willing to add selected financial names while reducing exposure to utilities, industrials and plantation stocks at the sector level. The report does not provide evidence of currency hedging or a specific global-allocation strategy, but the overall outflow trend signals continued caution.
Why Are the Three Groups So Different?
The gap may come down to investor type. Retail investors can react faster to stock stories and short-term price movements. Local institutions may rotate between large-cap names while balancing portfolio requirements. Foreign investors, meanwhile, remain influenced by wider regional fund flows, global inflation concerns and risk sentiment.
Risks to Watch
The biggest near-term risk is still inflation. Higher US energy costs pushed both consumer and producer prices higher, while Brent crude moved above US$109 per barrel. If energy prices stay elevated, pressure on global interest-rate expectations and equity valuations could increase.
Regional fund flows are another concern. Foreign investors continued to pull money from Asian equities, while Indonesia’s proposed MSCI index removal added to market uncertainty. For Malaysia, continued foreign selling—especially in utilities, industrials and plantation stocks—could keep trading conditions volatile.
For now, Bursa Malaysia is seeing an interesting tug-of-war: foreign funds are stepping back, but local retail investors are still willing to buy.

title: Malaysia Morning Wrap | US Stocks Fall on AI Spending Worries; Malaysia Eyes Palm Oil Duty Relief
author: Moomoo News MY
body:
📌 Key Takeaways
• US stocks fell as AI spending concerns and inflation worries resurfaced
• Nasdaq dropped 1.38% at close; S&P 500 lost 0.30%
• KLCI slipped 0.17% at close; USD/MYR eased to 4.0595
• Malaysia studies palm oil duty exemption; Tencent Cloud plans investment
• Stocks to Watch: ZETRIX, YTLPOWR, etc.
🇺🇸 Wall Street Summary
$S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ 7,720.39(-0.30%)
$Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ 52,342.56(-0.25%)
$Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ 26,184.72(-1.38%)
U.S. stocks closed lower on Thursday, with the three major indexes snapping three-day winning streaks as weak reactions to earnings from large-cap names and renewed concerns over AI spending weighed on sentiment. The $Nasdaq Composite Index (.IXIC.US)$ shed 365.13 points (1.4%) to 26,184.72, the $S&P 500 Index (.SPX.US)$ lost 23.59 points (0.3%) to 7,720.39, and the $Dow Jones Industrial Average (.DJI.US)$ gave up 132.54 points (0.25%) to 52,342.56. Inflation worries also resurfaced after the U.S. Commerce Department said Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annual rate, above the 3.1% forecast, while the Labor Department reported September PCE inflation at 3.6%, still well above the Fed's 2% target.
$ServiceNow (NOW.US)$ plunged 27% after missing Q3 adjusted earnings estimates and guiding Q4 subscription revenue below forecasts, while $Alphabet-A (GOOGL.US)$ slumped 12.6% as negative Q3 free cash flow and softer revenue raised concerns over AI-related spending. $Marvell Technology (MRVL.US)$ dropped 13.2% after Bloomberg News reported it is in talks to acquire $Lumentum (LITE.US)$, while $Fortinet (FTNT.US)$ fell 20.1% after cutting full-year service-revenue guidance and $Caterpillar (CAT.US)$ lost 9.3% on weak construction-industries sales. Among the Magnificent Seven, $Amazon (AMZN.US)$ fell 4.3%, $NVIDIA (NVDA.US)$ slipped 0.8%, while $Meta Platforms (META.US)$ rose 2% and $Apple (AAPL.US)$ gained 1.5%.

Top Loser: $PCHEM (5183.MY)$ RM4.570 (-3.18%)
USD/MYR: $USD/MYR (USDMYR.FX)$ 4.0595(-0.43%)
Malaysia is consulting palm oil industry players on a proposed crude palm oil export duty exemption, a policy move that could affect export flows and cost structures across the sector. The development is being monitored as Malaysia remains one of the world's key palm oil exporters.
Tencent Cloud said it will invest in Malaysia over the next three years, adding to ongoing foreign direct investment interest in the country's digital infrastructure and cloud ecosystem. Separately, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim urged mid-tier listed companies to scale up and expand regionally, highlighting the government's push to build larger Malaysian corporates.
Kenanga Investment Bank raised its 2026 Malaysia producer price inflation forecast to 7.4%, pointing to a firmer cost environment outlook. In global commodities, oil market volatility remained elevated amid the Iran war, with supply concerns keeping energy markets in focus.

🔔 Stocks to Watch
$ZETRIX (0138.MY)$ said a dissolution event has been triggered, but no immediate repayment is required on RM2.16 billion of notes. In a separate development, the government filed a suit and issued a RM353.13 million tax bill to a MyEG-linked unit under the group, marking a material legal and regulatory update.
$SDG (5285.MY)$ and $YTLPOWR (6742.MY)$ are partnering with Bumi Assets to develop a 1,623-acre industrial park in Klang, Selangor. The proposed project adds a large-scale industrial and infrastructure development to both companies' current pipelines.
$MAYBANK (1155.MY)$ launched a ringgit account for Singapore corporate clients to support cross-border banking needs. The product expansion broadens the bank's regional offering for business customers handling Malaysia-related transactions.
$BURSA (1818.MY)$ remained on track for its FY2026 targets after 3Q earnings came in in line with consensus estimates. The exchange operator's update indicates no change to its stated full-year direction.
$GENTING (3182.MY)$ said it has no plans for further fundraising for now, even as debt repayment obligations remain in focus. The company's latest capital management update centres on funding plans and upcoming repayment commitments.
$HTPADU (5028.MY)$ said it is no longer working with Zetrix AI on the NIISe project, but stated the change will not have any impact on project delivery. The company described the development as an operational update without material effect on the project.
$JFTECH (0146.MY)$ proposed an issuance of up to 388 million free warrants to reward shareholders. The corporate exercise would alter the company's capital structure if implemented.
$AXREIT (5106.MY)$ reported third-quarter net property income fell 2.8% year on year, while net profit increased. The results reflect mixed quarterly performance across its core property and bottom-line metrics.
$BAT (4162.MY)$ posted a 66.5% decline in third-quarter net profit, with higher cost of sales cited as a key factor. The earnings update reflects margin pressure during the quarter.
$TAGHILL (0241.MY)$ secured a RM166 million contract for a commercial building project in Penang. The award adds to the group's order book and represents a fresh construction job in the current financial period.
$TSH (9059.MY)$ said it found no business links to the 10 Indonesian firms named by Singapore's National Environment Agency. The plantation group issued the clarification in response to external scrutiny tied to the listed entities.
